statement.name: Closed Lipschitz determinacy
statement.definition: Determinacy of Lipschitz games G_L(A,B) with A,B Π01 (closed sets of the Baire space).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5), also to (Δ01,Π01)-DetL and (Δ01,Σ01∧Π01)-SLOL; ATR0 proves Π01-DetL and (Δ01,Σ01∧Π01)-DetL (Proposition 3).

statement.name: Lipschitz determinacy with clopen and closed payoffs
statement.definition: Determinacy of G_L(A,B) with A Δ01 and B Π01.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5); it implies ACA0 over RCA0 (proof of (3)=>(1)).

statement.name: Lipschitz semilinear ordering for clopen and difference-of-open sets
statement.definition: Red_L(A,B) or Red_L(not B,A) for A in Δ01 and B in Σ01∧Π01.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5); implies ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Weak comparability of countable well orderings
statement.definition: For all countable well orderings α,β there is an order-preserving injection of one into the other (α ≤w β or β ≤w α).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3, cited from Hirst, Theorem 4 of [5]).

statement.name: Existence of rank functions for well-founded trees
statement.definition: Every well-founded tree T in N^{<N} has a rank function (rk, α) with α a countable well ordering.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4, essentially Theorem 7 of Hirst [4]).

statement.name: Nonstandard counterpart of WWKL0
statement.definition: System of nonstandard second-order arithmetic: ns-BASIC (standard part RCA0, embedding and end extension principles, Sigma^0_1 overspill, Sigma^0_1/Sigma^1_0 equivalence, Delta^0_0 transfer) plus the Loeb measure property LMP (if a nonstandard tree has positive Loeb measure, its standard part has a path).
statement.facts: ns-WWKL0 proves WWKL in the standard universe (Theorem 3.4) and is a conservative extension of WWKL0 (Theorem 3.5). LMP is equivalent over ns-BASIC to the Loeb-measure forms of Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.5; ns-WWKL0 proves countable subadditivity of Lebesgue measure, Riemann integrability of bounded continuous functions and a monotone convergence form of Ascoli's lemma (Lemma 4.7). Also: ns-BASIC is conservative over RCA0 (Theorem 2.4) and ns-WKL0 over WKL0 (Theorem 2.6); LMP is not implied by ns-BASIC plus any true L2 sentence (Remark 3.8).

statement.name: Loeb measure property
statement.definition: If a nonstandard binary tree T* has positive Loeb measure at some nonstandard length omega, then there is a standard function f: N -> 2 with f[n] in T* for all standard n.
statement.facts: Nonstandard counterpart of WWKL; over ns-BASIC it is equivalent to the statements of Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.5 (standard part of positive Loeb measure sets, Loeb measure of st^{-1} of open sets, integral as standard part of nonstandard Riemann sums).

statement.name: Existence of a set of Archimedean representatives for an ordered abelian group
statement.definition: For an ordered abelian group G, Archimedean equivalence a ≈ b means there are n, m with |na| ≥ |b| and |mb| ≥ |a|. A set X ⊂ G is a set of Archimedean representatives if every g in G is Archimedean equivalent to some x in X and distinct elements of X are not Archimedean equivalent. The statement: every ordered abelian group has such a set.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.3: over RCA0, for any ordered abelian group G (the proof uses a computable such G), ACA0 is equivalent to the existence of a set of Archimedean representatives for G. Lemma 3.2: over RCA0 this is equivalent to the existence of the set {<g,h> | g ≈ h}. Corollary 3.4: there is a computable ordered abelian group for which every set of Archimedean representatives computes 0'.

statement.name: Hahn's embedding theorem for ordered abelian groups
statement.loc: Section 4, Hahn's Theorem (formal version) before Theorem 4.4
statement.definition: For every ordered abelian group G there are a linear order T and a sequence of Archimedean ordered subgroups K_t (t in T) of G such that G is order isomorphic to a Hahn subgroup (a subgroup of the unrestricted sum of the K_t with the cut property, all supports well ordered, ordered reverse lexicographically) of the sum over T of K_t.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.4: over RCA0, Hahn's Theorem is equivalent to ACA0. Proposition 4.5 proves the reversal (Hahn's Theorem implies ACA0 over RCA0); Section 5 proves Hahn's Theorem in ACA0.

statement.notation: Every torsion free abelian group is orderable
statement.name: Orderability of torsion free abelian groups
statement.definition: Every torsion free abelian group admits a linear order compatible with the group operation (an ordered abelian group structure).
statement.facts: Theorem 1.2 (Hatzikiriakou, Simpson, cited): over RCA0 this is equivalent to WKL0. Theorem 1.1 (Downey, Kurtz): there is a computable torsion free abelian group with no computable order.

statement.name: Holder's theorem for Archimedean ordered groups
statement.definition: Every Archimedean ordered group is isomorphic to an ordered subgroup of (R, +) indexed by the group, for which +A and <=A are the group operation and order.
statement.facts: Stated as provable in RCA0 (citing Solomon [9] for the proof).

statement.name: Complement of a divisible subgroup of an abelian group
statement.definition: If D is a divisible subgroup of an abelian group G, then G = D + A for some subgroup A.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.14 (cited from Simpson, Lemma VI.4.2): provable in ACA0.

statement.name: Stable ascending/descending chain principle (type ω+ω*)
statement.definition: Every stable linear order L (with domain a subset of ω) with infinitely many small and infinitely many large elements has an infinite ascending or descending chain.
statement.facts: SADC ≤sW SADS and SADC ≤sW General-ADC; computable instances of SADC have low solutions (per the proof of Theorem 17(3)); General-ADC ≰W SADS (Theorem 17(2)). The catalogue entry sadc ("every infinite stable linear order has ...") may correspond to the paper's General-ADC rather than to this SADC.

statement.name: ADS for stable linear orders (any stable order)
statement.definition: Every stable linear order L (every element small or large; type ω+k, k+ω* or ω+ω*) has an infinite ascending or descending sequence.
statement.facts: SADS ≤sW General-ADS ≤sW ADS; ADC ≰W General-ADS (Theorem 17(3)); equivalent to ADS, SADS, SADC, General-ADC under ≤c.

statement.name: ADC for stable linear orders (any stable order)
statement.definition: Every stable linear order L has an infinite ascending or descending chain.
statement.facts: SADC ≤sW General-ADC ≤sW ADC and General-ADC ≤sW General-ADS; General-ADC ≰W SADS (Theorem 17(2)). Possibly the catalogue sadc.

statement.notation: Every set is contained in a countable coded ω-model of ACA
statement.name: Existence of countable coded ω-models of ACA containing a given set
statement.definition: For every set X there is a countable coded ω-model M = (N,S,∈,+,·,0,1,<) with S = {(W)_n : n in N} of arithmetic comprehension (ACA) such that X in S (Definition 3.3).
statement.facts: Lemma 3.4: over RCA0 it is equivalent to the ω-jump axiom of ACA0+ (every set X has an ω-jump Y with (Y)_0 = X and (Y)_{n+1} = TJ((Y)_n)). Theorem 4.1: RCA0 + ∀X[WO(X) → WO(εX)] proves it.

statement.name: Weak König's lemma for trees defined by bounded formulae
statement.definition: Scheme Tree∞(A_x) → ∃X (Path(X) ∧ ∀x (x ∈ X → A(x))) for A a bounded (Σb∞) formula, over binary words 2^{<ω}; every infinite tree of 0-1 words defined by a bounded formula has an infinite path.
statement.facts: Σb1-NIA + ∇b1-CA + Σb∞-WKL is Π02-conservative over Σb1-NIA (Theorem 2). Σb1-NIA + Σb∞-WKL proves BΣb∞ (Proposition 5); the first-order part of Σb1-NIA + ∇b1-CA + Σb∞-WKL is Σb1-NIA + BΣb∞ (Theorem 7); the theory is Π11-conservative over Σb1-NIA + ∇b1-CA + BΣb∞ (Corollary 9); BTFA + Σb∞-WKL is Π11-conservative over BTFA (Theorem 10 ii). This is a bounded-arithmetic setting (binary words, polynomial-time functions), not WKL over RCA0.

statement.name: Collection scheme for bounded formulae
statement.definition: ∀x ≤ a ∃y A(x,y) → ∃z ∀x ≤ a ∃y ≤ z A(x,y), A a bounded formula (equivalent over Σb1-NIA to the variant (S2) with x ≡ a).
statement.facts: Σb1-NIA + BΣb∞ is conservative over Σb1-NIA for Π02-sentences (Corollary 6); it is exactly the first-order strength of Σb∞-WKL (Theorem 7).

statement.name: Base Theory for Feasible Analysis
statement.definition: Σb1-NIA + BΣb∞ + the comprehension scheme ($): ∀x (∃y A(x,y) ↔ ∀z ¬B(x,z)) → ∃X ∀x (x ∈ X ↔ ∃y A(x,y)), A, B Σb1.
statement.facts: BTFA is Π02-conservative over Σb1-NIA (Theorem 10 i); BTFA + Σb∞-WKL is Π11-conservative over BTFA (Theorem 10 ii); (2^{<ω}, Δ01) is its smallest model with standard first-order part.

statement.name: NP ∩ co-NP comprehension
statement.definition: ∀x (A(x) ↔ ¬B(x)) → ∃X ∀x (x ∈ X ↔ A(x)) for Σb1 formulae A, B with parameters.
statement.facts: Σb1-NIA + ∇b1-CA is first-order conservative over Σb1-NIA (Lemma 1).

statement.name: Notation induction axiom for Σb1 formulae (binary tree theory, equivalent to Buss' S^1_2)
statement.definition: Basic axioms on the language (ε, 0, 1, concatenation, x×y, initial subword) plus induction on notation A(ε) ∧ ∀x (A(x) → A(x0) ∧ A(x1)) → ∀x A(x) for Σb1 formulae A.
statement.facts: Provably total Σb1-definable functions are the polynomial-time computable functions; base theory of the paper.

statement.name: Universal transfer principle of ERNA
statement.definition: For quantifier-free phi(x) in the standard language of ERNA: (forall^st x) phi(x) -> (forall x) phi(x).
statement.facts: Equivalent in ERNA to bar transfer (Theorem 8), to the continuity and equicontinuity principles (Theorems 18, 19), and to the sequential nonstandard versions of IVT, MVT, IMV, the Weierstrass extremum theorem and the Peano existence theorem (Theorems 23, 26, 28, 39, 40, 46, 50, 53); these are results in ERNA (a nonstandard system over I Delta0 + exp), not over RCA0.

statement.name: Sequential mean value theorem
statement.definition: For a sequence of functions phi_n continuous on [0,1], differentiable on (0,1) with phi_n(0)=phi_n(1)=0, there is a sequence x_n in [0,1] with phi_n'(x_n) = 0 for all n.
statement.facts: Stated to be equivalent to WKL0 (due to T. Yamazaki, unpublished); the paper also notes MVT is provable in RCA0 by Hardin and Velleman [11, Theorem 4].

statement.notation: every countable poset has a maximal filter
statement.name: Existence of maximal filters on countable posets
statement.definition: Every countable poset has a filter (upward closed, any two elements have a common lower bound in the filter) that is not contained in a strictly larger filter.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Corollaries 2.2 and 2.4, from Theorems 2.1 and 2.3). Computable version: every computable poset has a Delta^0_2 maximal filter (Thm 2.1), there is a computable poset with no Sigma^0_1 or Pi^0_1 maximal filter (Thm 2.5), and one on which every maximal filter computes 0' (Thm 2.3, 0' <=wtt F).

statement.notation: every countable poset has an unbounded filter
statement.name: Existence of unbounded filters on countable posets
statement.definition: Every countable poset has a filter F such that no p outside F is a lower bound of all elements of F.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Corollary 3.3, from Theorem 3.2). Computable version: every computable poset has a Sigma^0_1 unbounded filter (Thm 3.1), there is one with no Pi^0_1 unbounded filter (Thm 3.4), and one on which every unbounded filter computes 0' (Thm 3.2). RCA0 proves every countable poset has an unbounded enumerated filter.

statement.notation: extension of sequences of enumerated filters to unbounded enumerated filters
statement.name: Uniform extension of enumerated filters to unbounded enumerated filters
statement.definition: If <P_i> is a sequence of countable posets and each F_i is an enumerated filter on P_i (a function from N to P whose range is a filter), then there is a sequence <G_i> with G_i an unbounded enumerated filter on P_i extending F_i.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.6). The single-poset version (every enumerated filter on a countable poset extends to an unbounded enumerated filter) is provable in RCA0 (Theorem 3.5).

statement.notation: every subset of a countable poset has an upward closure
statement.name: Existence of upward closures in countable posets
statement.definition: For every subset F of a countable poset P, the set {q in P : exists p in F, p <= q} exists. Also considered for linearly ordered subsets F only.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0, and also to the version restricted to linearly ordered subsets (Corollary 4.2, from Theorem 4.1: a computable poset with a computable linearly ordered subset whose upward closure one-one computes 0').

statement.name: Pouzet's theorem on better binary relations
statement.definition: For every binary relation R on a countable set Q there is a partial ordering contained in R which is bqo if and only if R is a better binary relation (every Q-array is good with respect to R); the map R to the ordering is continuous.
statement.facts: Proved in the paper with Simpson's Borel-array definition of bqo, using the minimal bad array lemma (Theorem 2.12) and Galvin-Prikry (Theorem 2.4). Used to reduce bbr to bqo in the proof that BQO is Pi^1_2-complete. Not a reverse-mathematics fact (no base system is considered).

statement.name: Weak König's lemma over the weak base IΣ00 + exp
statement.definition: The theory consisting of IΣ00 + exp, Δ01 comprehension and Weak König's Lemma (the base RCA*0 plus WKL).
statement.facts: Corollary 3: there is an interpretation of WKL*0 in IΔ0 + exp. Also cited (Simpson-Smith, Theorem 4.6): every countable model of BΣ1 + exp expands to a model of WKL*0; it is open whether there is an omega-interpretation of WKL*0 in BΣ1 + exp, and whether WKL*0 has at most polynomial speed-up over IΔ0 + exp.

statement.notation: Free product of f.o. groups is fully orderable
statement.name: Free products of fully ordered groups are fully orderable
statement.definition: The free product A * B of two fully ordered (f.o.) countable groups A and B is fully orderable.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 (Theorem 5 and Theorem 16). Corollary 17: RCA0 proves the free group on two generators is fully orderable; Proposition 21: RCA0 proves the free group on countably many generators is fully orderable.

statement.notation: Every countable f.o. group is an o-epimorphic image of an f.o. free group
statement.name: Fully ordered groups are quotients of fully ordered free groups
statement.definition: Every countable f.o. group is the o-epimorphic image of a fully ordered free group; equivalently it is o-isomorphic to F/N for a fully ordered free group F and a convex normal subgroup N.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 (Theorem 4 and Theorem 22), via Theorem 16 and a technique of Revesz.

statement.notation: Infinite direct product of f.o. groups is fully orderable
statement.name: Fully orderability of infinite direct products of fully orderable groups
statement.loc: Section 1, paragraph after Definition 6 and Theorem 7
statement.definition: The restricted direct product of an infinite (not uniformly ordered) sequence of fully orderable groups is fully orderable.
statement.facts: Stated in Section 1 (citing Solomon [9]) to be equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 in general; with a uniform sequence of orders RCA0 suffices to order it lexicographically. Not a result proved in this paper.

statement.notation: Induced order on G/H for p.o. group G and convex normal H
statement.name: Existence of the induced order on a quotient group
statement.definition: For a convex normal subgroup H of an ordered group G, the induced order on G/H exists.
statement.facts: For p.o. groups, ACA0 is required (cited from Solomon [9]); for f.o. groups RCA0 suffices (Theorem 2).

statement.notation: Saturation lemma for intuitionistic predicate logic
statement.name: Saturation lemma for intuitionistic logic (predicate and propositional with countably many atoms)
statement.definition: If a sentence sigma_0 is not intuitionistically deducible from a theory Gamma and C is an infinite set of new constants, then there is a C-saturated theory Gamma' in L(C) (not intuitionistically proving falsum, deductively closed, with the disjunction property and the existence property with witnesses in C) containing Gamma and not deducing sigma_0.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.3: over RCA_0, WKL_0 is equivalent to the saturation lemma for intuitionistic predicate logic and to the saturation lemma for intuitionistic propositional logic with countably many atoms. The proof is analogous to the one for the completeness theorem of classical logic in Simpson's book, Section 4.3. Neither principle is in the catalogue as such (the catalogue's completeness entry is Goedel's theorem for classical logic).

statement.notation: Strong completeness theorem for intuitionistic predicate logic
statement.name: Strong completeness theorem for intuitionistic logic (predicate and propositional with countably many atoms)
statement.definition: For every intuitionistically consistent countable theory Gamma there is a Kripke model (K, <=_K, forcing) coded as a set such that for every sentence sigma, Gamma proves sigma intuitionistically iff every world of K forces sigma (the theory is characterized by a single Kripke model).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.7: over RCA_0, ACA_0 is equivalent to the strong completeness theorem for intuitionistic predicate logic and to the strong completeness theorem for intuitionistic propositional logic with countably many atoms; the reversal derives Sigma^0_1 comprehension from the propositional version. Not in the catalogue.

statement.notation: L-maximal theory with respect to sigma_0; Lemma 3.3
statement.name: Existence of maximal extensions for intuitionistic theories
statement.definition: If sigma_0 is not intuitionistically deducible from Gamma, there is an L(C)-maximal theory Gamma' with respect to sigma_0 extending Gamma (consistent with sigma_0, deductively closed, disjunction and existence properties, and containing every sentence sigma with Gamma' + sigma not proving sigma_0).
statement.facts: Lemma 3.3 and its refinement Lemma 3.5 are proved in ACA_0 (auxiliary lemmas, used for the strong completeness theorem; no reversal stated for them).

statement.notation: Every non-empty closed subset of a compact complete separable metric space is separably closed
statement.name: Closed subsets of compact complete separable metric spaces are separably closed
statement.definition: Closed sets are complements of unions of open balls (coded by the codes of their complements); separably closed sets are closures of countable sets of points. The statement says every non-empty closed subset of a compact (Simpson, Definition III.2.3) complete separable metric space is separably closed.
statement.facts: Theorem 1: over RCA0, equivalent to ACA0 (and to statement (3) below). (1) implies (2) is Theorem 3.2 of Brown [2]; the paper gives the corrected proof that (3) implies (1) via the monotone convergence theorem for sequences of rationals in (0,1).

statement.notation: Every non-empty closed subset of [0,1] is separably closed
statement.name: Closed subsets of [0,1] are separably closed
statement.definition: Special case of the previous statement for the compact complete separable metric space [0,1]: every non-empty closed subset of [0,1] (coded by the codes of its complement) is the closure of a countable sequence of points.
statement.facts: Theorem 1: over RCA0, equivalent to ACA0 and to statement (2); (2) implies (3) because RCA0 proves [0,1] is a compact complete separable metric space; the reversal (3) implies ACA0 is proved (corrected proof) through the monotone convergence theorem for increasing sequences of rationals in (0,1), using closed set [0, lim a_n].

statement.name: Every automorphism of a countable dense linear order without endpoints has k-th roots (Property 1 of Theorem 1.6)
statement.definition: For every automorphism f of Q and every k >= 1 there is an automorphism g with g^k = f.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0 (classical proof defining automorphisms uniformly on orbitals, Section 2); not provable in RCA0 because Theorem 4.1 gives a computable f with no computable k-th root for any k >= 2. Whether WKL0 suffices and whether there is a reversal to WKL0 or ACA0 is left open.

statement.notation: Every automorphism of Q is a commutator [f,g] of itself with some g (Property 2 of Theorem 1.6)
statement.name: Stronger commutator property of Aut(Q)
statement.definition: For every automorphism f of Q there is an automorphism g with f = [f,g].
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0 via Property 3; not provable in RCA0 (Theorem 5.5 gives a computable f with f != [f,h] for all computable h). WKL0 status open, no known reversals.

statement.notation: Conjugacy iff isomorphic orbital structures (Property 3 of Theorem 1.6)
statement.name: Conjugacy of automorphisms of Q by orbital structure
statement.definition: Two automorphisms of Q are conjugate iff their orbital structures are isomorphic.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0 (uses orbital equivalence, which is arithmetical); fails for computable automorphisms (Corollary 5.10), hence not provable in RCA0. Also, every element of Aut_c(Q) is a commutator, provable in RCA0 (Theorem 5.4).

statement.name: Intersection point problem for an injective path
statement.definition: The operator which, given continuous paths f, g : [0;1] -> [0;1]^2 satisfying (3) and (4) of Theorem 1.4 with f injective, finds a point of intersection of range(f) and range(g) (the uniform problem of Theorem 6.1).
statement.facts: The paper states, citing Brattka, Gherardi and Pauly (Theorem 7.34 of arXiv:1707.03202), that CC_[0;1] (connected choice, catalogue ivt/ci) is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to IVP (intermediate value problem, catalogue ivt) and to IP1. The paper itself proves no Weihrauch fact; Theorem 1.3 and Theorem 1.4 are computability results (computable paths have a computable point of intersection) and the degree of the general intersection operator is stated to be not yet located in the Weihrauch lattice.

statement.name: Dini's theorem (for a metric space X; DT for all compact metric spaces, DT_{0,1}^N, DT_[0,1])
statement.definition: If a monotone sequence (f_n) of continuous functions on X converges simply to a continuous function f on X, then (f_n) converges uniformly to f. Continuity on a compact metric space includes a modulus of uniform continuity (Bishop).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.8: over Bishop-style constructive mathematics (within EL + AC00), the following are equivalent: the fan theorem for detachable bars FT (catalogue fandelta), DT for the Cantor space, DT for all compact metric spaces, DT for [0,1] (Corollary 4.5, Propositions 4.2, 4.4, 4.6, 4.7). FT already follows from DT on Cantor space for functions with values in {0,1}. Theorem 5.2: over RCA0, DT_X for all compact metric spaces X is equivalent to WKL. The constructive equivalences are proved in EL + AC00 (full induction), not in EL0, so they are not entered over el0 or bish.

statement.name: Classical contrapositive of weak Konig's lemma (every tree without infinite path is finite)
statement.definition: Every (detachable binary) tree without infinite path is finite: forall alpha exists n (alpha|n not in T) implies exists N forall alpha (alpha|N not in T).
statement.facts: Lemma 5.1: WKL¬ and FT are equivalent (constructively, within EL + AC00). The paper also recalls (citing Ishihara, reference [8]) that WKL implies FT over EL.

statement.name: Separating hyperplane theorem for a convex closed located set and a convex hull of finitely many vectors (Hilbert space)
statement.definition: Let (H, <,>) be a Hilbert space and C a convex, closed, located subset of H. If x_1,...,x_n are in H and C is disjoint from the convex hull C(x_1,...,x_n), then there are eps > 0 and p in H with <p, x - c> >= eps for all x in C(x_1,...,x_n) and c in C. Constructive statement.
statement.facts: Proposition 2: SEP, FTAP and MP are equivalent in constructive mathematics (over BISH). Remark 2: the authors claim SEP and FTAP are provable in RCA0, since no non-constructive choice is used and MP holds classically (an informal claim, not a theorem). Remark 1: SEP and FTAP are true in recursive constructive mathematics. The paper notes that the Hahn-Banach theorem implies SEP (Hahn-Banach is classified into WKL by Brown-Simpson).

statement.name: Fundamental theorem of asset pricing (non-trivial direction, finite market)
statement.definition: For every real m x n matrix A with linearly independent rows: if {xi . A : xi in R^m} intersected with Y_n is empty (no arbitrage; Y_n = nonnegative vectors with positive sum), then there is p in P_n (strictly positive coordinates summing to 1) with A . p = 0 (an equivalent martingale measure).
statement.facts: Proposition 2: FTAP is equivalent to SEP and to Markov's principle MP in constructive mathematics. Corollary 3: constructive version with the hypothesis d(xi . A, x) > 0 for all xi, x in X_n. Remark 2: claimed provable in RCA0 (informal).

statement.name: Uniformly continuous convex positive-valued functions on convex hulls of finitely many vectors have positive infimum
statement.definition: Every uniformly continuous convex function f : X_m -> R+ (X_m the standard simplex), or more generally f : C(A_1,...,A_m) -> R+ on the convex hull of finitely many points of a normed space, has inf f > 0. A constructive strengthening for convex functions of the fan-theorem-type principle FAN (every uniformly continuous f : [0,1] -> R+ has positive infimum; the catalogue's posinf).
statement.facts: Proved constructively (Proposition 1, by induction on m) with no omniscience principle; it is used to derive MP -> SEP. The paper notes that FAN can be deduced from LLPO (citing Ishihara) and that the Hahn-Banach theorem is equivalent to LLPO (citing Ishihara 1990).

statement.notation: rank function existence (every countable well founded directed graph has a rank function)
statement.name: Existence of rank functions for well founded directed graphs
statement.definition: A rank function for a directed acyclic graph G is a pair <f, alpha>, alpha well ordering, f maps V onto alpha, (u,v) in E implies f(u)<f(v), and for x<f(v) there is u with (u,v) in E and x<=f(u). G is well founded if no infinite sequence has (v_{j+1},v_j) an edge for all j.
statement.facts: Theorem 5: ATR0 proves it; Theorem 7: equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0; Theorem 1: RCA0 proves it for finite directed acyclic graphs; Theorem 2: RCA0 proves a graph with a rank function is well founded.

statement.notation: rank functions for arbitrary directed graphs (value infinity)
statement.name: Cantor-Bendixson style rank function for all directed graphs
statement.definition: For every directed graph G there is <f, alpha> with alpha a well ordering, f:V -> alpha U {infinity}, f a rank function on the preimage of alpha, and every vertex with f(u)=infinity has a predecessor v with f(v)=infinity.
statement.facts: Theorem 8: equivalent to Pi^1_1-CA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Uniqueness of rank functions
statement.definition: Any two rank functions of the same countable graph induce the same order and equalities on vertices; their well orderings are isomorphic via a unique order preserving bijection h with h(f(v))=g(v).
statement.facts: All provable in RCA0.

statement.notation: path bounded graphs and rank functions bounded by N (or by n)
statement.name: Bounded rank functions
statement.definition: G is path bounded if for each pair of vertices v,u the paths from v to u have length at most some integer; uniformly path bounded if one integer works for all pairs. A rank function is bounded by beta if its ordering is an initial segment of beta.
statement.facts: Theorem 14: over RCA0, ACA0 is equivalent to 'G is path bounded iff G has a rank function bounded by N' and to the uniform version with some n in N.

statement.name: Slow well-partial-ordering assertion (finite miniaturization of WPO(C) with logarithmic weight growth)
statement.definition: For a class C of iterated finite sequences or ordered trees with weight |.| and the iterated homeomorphic embedding with symmetric gap condition E: for every K there is M such that every x_0..x_M in C with |x_i| < K + log_a(i+1) for all i has i<j with x_i E x_j.
statement.facts: Phase transitions (Theorem 1, Corollary 2): for the triples (PA, S^2, 1/2), (Delta11-CA, S^3, 1/3), (Pi01-CA_{<phi^(d)(0)}, S^{d+1}, 1/(d+1)), (Pi11-CA0, TS^1=TT^1, (sqrt17-1)/8), (Delta12-CA, TS^2, (sqrt5-1)/4), (Pi11-CA_{<phi^(d)(0)}, TS^d, (sqrt(d^2+16)-d)/8) and (Pi11-CA0^(d), TT^d, (sqrt17-1)/8): SWP(C,1/r) is provable in T for r<t and unprovable for r>t. Limit versions for ATR0 and Pi11-TR0. The paper only treats provability of arithmetical (miniaturized) sentences in theories T (proof theory), not comparisons among catalogue statements.

statement.name: Solecki dichotomy (Theorem 1.4, weaker versions 1.6 and 1.8)
statement.definition: For every Borel function f : omega^omega -> omega^omega, either f is sigma-continuous (a countable union of partial continuous functions) or the Turing jump J reduces to f (topologically embeds in Thm 1.4; reducible via partial continuous phi, psi with f = psi(g(phi(x))) in Thm 1.6; weakly reducible, i.e. continuous Weihrauch reducible J <=_w f where psi may also use x, in Thm 1.8).
statement.facts: Theorem 1.8 (weak version) is shown equivalent to the cone version of the Posner-Robinson theorem (Theorem 1.12): Posner-Robinson + Borel determinacy implies Theorem 1.8 (Section 2); Theorem 1.8 + Pi^1_1-determinacy implies Theorem 1.12 (Section 3). Generalised version for alpha-th jump (Theorems 4.2, 4.5) behaves the same.

statement.name: Posner-Robinson theorem (Theorems 1.9, 1.10, cone version 1.12)
statement.definition: For every real x, either x is computable or there is y with x (+) y >=_T y'. Relativized: for all z, x, either x <=_T z or some y has x (+) y (+) z >=_T (y (+) z)'. Cone version: there is a cone of Turing degrees C such that the relativized statement holds for every z in C.
statement.facts: Equivalent, in the sense above, to the weak Solecki dichotomy (Theorem 1.8), using Borel determinacy in one direction and Pi^1_1-determinacy in the other; generalized to higher jumps (Theorems 4.3, 4.4, 4.6).

statement.name: Determinacy principles (Theorems 1.13, 1.14)
statement.definition: Borel determinacy: G(A) is determined for Borel A; analytic (Pi^1_1) determinacy follows from a measurable cardinal; AD for all sets. Used as set-theoretic tools only (ZFC and large cardinals), not studied in reverse mathematics.
statement.facts: No reverse-mathematics or Weihrauch results about them in the paper.

statement.name: Weak Konig's lemma with weak uniqueness hypothesis
statement.definition: For detachable subtrees of the binary fan: if for every y there is a path of length y in the tree, and any two infinite paths of the tree are equal (the weak form of at most one path: forall alpha,beta in the tree, alpha = beta), then the tree has an infinite path.
statement.facts: WKL entails WKL!! which entails WKL! (equivalent to FTd), hence FTd; M + FTd does not prove WKL!! (Proposition 19), because WKL!! is constructively equivalent to MP-or plus not-not-WKL and every theorem of M + FTd is G-realizable while MP-or is not (cited [14]); M + BId does not prove WKL!!, and M + BId + WKL!! does not prove WKL (announced).

statement.name: Bar induction with decidable bar
statement.definition: Kleene's bar induction schema: forall alpha exists x R(alpha-bar(x)) and R decidable and R implies A and (forall s A(w*<s>)) implies A(w) give A(<>). Interderivable with the variants BI!, BImu and BIf over IA1 or M.
statement.facts: FTd is a constructive consequence of BId, but not conversely (the arithmetical functions are a realizability model of M + FTd but not of M + BId, Section 5.1); BImon (monotone bar) entails BI! over M.

statement.name: Countable function comprehension (unique choice)
statement.definition: forall x exists! y A(x,y) implies exists alpha forall x A(x, alpha(x)); the axiom added to IA1 to get Kleene's minimal system M.
statement.facts: Equivalent over IA1 to AC01! and to the least-number form ACmu00; IA1 + CFd does not prove AC00! (Theorem 1); over IA1 + CFd, QF-AC00 entails AC00! (Proposition 3); EL + CFd proves AC00! (Proposition 5).

statement.name: Characteristic function principle for decidable predicates
statement.definition: forall x (B(x) or not B(x)) implies there is beta with beta(x) <= 1 and (beta(x) = 0 iff B(x)).
statement.facts: Consequence of AC00! over IA1; IA1 + QF-AC00 does not prove CFd (Theorem 4); EL does not prove CFd (Proposition 6); IA1 + BC00 proves CFd (Proposition 10); M = IA1 + CFd + QF-AC00.

statement.name: Bounding axiom, monotone countable choice, bounded countable choice
statement.definition: AB00: forall x exists y A(x,y) implies exists beta forall x exists y <= beta(x) A(x,y). ACm00: countable choice for predicates monotone in y. BC00: forall x exists y <= beta(x) A(x,y) implies exists alpha forall x A(x, alpha(x)).
statement.facts: ACm00 and AB00 are equivalent over IA1 (Proposition 13); AC00 is equivalent to AB00 + BC00; IA1 + AB00 proves QF-AC00 (Proposition 12); M does not prove BC00 (Theorem 14); IA1 + BC00 does not prove AB00 or QF-AC00 (Proposition 11).

statement.name: Choice axiom for the binary fan
statement.definition: forall alpha in 2^N exists y R(alpha-bar(y)) implies exists sigma [forall alpha in 2^N exists! x sigma(alpha-bar(x)) = 0 and forall v in 2^* (sigma(v)=0 implies R(v))].
statement.facts: M + FT proves it (Proposition 18); FT and this schema are interderivable over M + FTd; FT is constructively equivalent over M to FTd + AB^2_{1/2,0} (Theorem 17).

statement.name: Kleene's minimal system of two-sorted intuitionistic analysis
statement.definition: IA1 (two-sorted intuitionistic arithmetic with full induction) plus AC00!.
statement.facts: Conservative over IA0 (Proposition 9); EL + CFd and M coincide up to translation (Theorem 7); M is strictly stronger than EL and than IA1 + QF-AC00 or IA1 + CFd.

statement.name: Feferman's system IR of predicative provability
statement.definition: Delta^1_1 Comprehension Rule, Hierarchy Rule and Transfinite Induction Rule (inference rules, not axioms).
statement.facts: IR and ATR0 have the same proof-theoretic ordinal Gamma_0 and prove the same Pi^1_1 sentences; minimum omega-model of IR is HYP(Gamma_0).

statement.notation: domain of a single-valued Borel set in the plane is Borel
statement.name: Borel domain of single-valued Borel sets
statement.definition: The domain of a single-valued Borel set in the plane is Borel.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Transfinite induction axiom (bar induction)
statement.definition: Transfinite induction along every well ordering for all formulas.
statement.facts: Includes IR and ATR0, stronger proof-theoretically (Howard ordinal); Sigma^1_1-TI0 = ATR0 + Sigma^1_1-IND.

statement.name: Minimum of the range of a sequence (MIN: ℕ^ℕ → ℕ, MIN(p) = min{p(i)})
statement.definition: Total function ℕ^ℕ → ℕ giving the minimum of the values of p. Not the sentence minprinciple of the catalogue.
statement.facts: Satz 2.6: MIN ≤2 C. Satz 2.7: Ω ≤2 MIN. Satz 2.8: MIN is not ≤2 Ω. Satz 2.19: MIN is C∞-stetig (needs n = p(0) calls of C). Satz 2.20: MIN is not Cn-stetig for any n. The reduction ≤2 is Weihrauch reducibility on total functions.

statement.name: Total sorting of a sequence of natural numbers
statement.definition: SORT: ℕ^ℕ → ℕ^ℕ lists the elements of p in increasing order with their multiplicities, dropping larger numbers when a smaller number occurs infinitely often. Differs from the catalogue's sort (binary sorting) and sort-nat (restricted domain).
statement.facts: Satz 3.2: SORT ≡2 C (Weihrauch equivalent to the characteristic function of the range, i.e. to the jump).

statement.name: Characteristic function of the range of a sequence (Stein's C)
statement.loc: Section 'C-stetige Funktionen' (Chapter I) and Chapter II
statement.definition: C(p)(n) = 0 iff n+1 occurs in p, else 1. Weihrauch equivalent to the Turing jump, so probably the catalogue's tj, but the paper does not say so.
statement.facts: Defines the C-hierarchy: Γ is Cn+1-stetig iff Γ = A∘C∘B∘Σ with Σ Cn-stetig. Satz 2.17: Cn+1 is not ≤2 Cn (finite parallel versions of C). Satz 2.21: C is not C∞-stetig. C is not ≤2 Ω (cited from Stein).

statement.notation: U, KON, KON2, MAX, MAX2, KB
statement.name: Infinite range, convergence, limit, existence of maximum, point of convergence of a sequence of naturals
statement.loc: Chapter IV: Definition 4.1 to Satz 4.11 (U defined in Chapter I)
statement.definition: U(p)=0 iff the range of p is infinite; KON(p)=0 iff p converges; KON2(p)=m+1 if p converges to m and 0 otherwise; MAX(p)=0 iff p has a maximum; MAX2(p)=max+1 or 0; KB(p) = index from which p is constant, +1, or 0.
statement.facts: U ≡2 KON (Satz 4.2), U ≡2 MAX (Satz 4.7), MAX2 ≡2 KON2 (Satz 4.9), KON2 ≤2 L (Satz 4.4), KB ≤2 MAX2 and U ≤2 KB (Satz 4.11). All are C2-stetig and not C-stetig, i.e. strictly between C and C2 in the paper's hierarchy; U ≤2 KON2 (Satz 4.5).

statement.name: Rationality of a real, density of a rational sequence
statement.definition: RAT(p)=0 iff ρ(p) is rational. DICHT(p)=0 iff the rationals enumerated by p are dense in ℝ.
statement.facts: Both are C2-stetig (reduce to N, the test for M_p = ℕ) and neither is C-stetig (U ≤2 RAT, U ≤2 DICHT).

statement.name: Existence of a constant subsequence, convergence of sequences of rationals or reals, existence of a convergent subsequence
statement.definition: T(p)=0 iff p has a constant subsequence; QKON (RKON) tests convergence of a sequence of rationals (reals); TQKON (TRKON) tests existence of a convergent subsequence of a sequence of rationals (reals).
statement.facts: T ≡2 QKON ≡2 RKON ≡2 TQKON ≡2 TRKON (Satz 5.9, 5.10, 5.12, 5.13, 5.15, 5.16, 5.18, 5.19). All are C3-stetig; T and QKON are not C2-stetig (Satz 5.7 via the self-application problem Kψ¹).

statement.name: Translation of r-adic into s-adic representation of reals in [0,1]
statement.definition: Function sending an r-adic expansion to the canonical s-adic expansion of the same real.
statement.facts: Satz 3.24: TRANS_rs is continuous iff every prime divisor of s divides r. Otherwise Ω ≤2 TRANS_rs (Satz 3.23) and TRANS_rs is not ≤2 Ω (Satz 3.26); TRANS_rs is C-stetig (Satz 3.25) and C is not ≤2 TRANS_rs (Satz 3.28).

statement.name: Continuation problem: partial function on sequences with infinitely many 1s, and its total extension
statement.definition: FSP(p)(i) is the parity of the position of the (i+1)-st 1 in p, defined only when p has infinitely many 1s. FS is a total extension with value 2 when undefined.
statement.facts: FSP has no continuous total extension (Satz 3.32); no total extension is ≤2 Ω (Satz 3.33); Ω ≤2 every total extension (Satz 3.37); FS is C-stetig (Satz 3.35) and C is not ≤2 FS (Satz 3.38); another extension FS2 satisfies C ≤2 FS2 (Satz 3.41).

statement.name: Longest path lemma
statement.definition: Every (detachable binary) tree T has a longest path: an infinite binary sequence alpha such that for all finite binary a, a in T implies alpha|a in T.
statement.facts: Proposition 2: LPL is equivalent to WKL over EL (full induction, not EL0). Used to prove WKL -> FAN_Delta (Theorem 3) over EL without Markov's principle. LPL is not in the catalogue.

statement.name: Fan theorem for detachable upward-closed bars (uniform form)
statement.definition: For every detachable upset B (not containing the empty sequence) which is a bar of Cantor space, there is n such that every binary sequence of length n lies in B.
statement.facts: Lemma 1: equivalent to FAN_Delta (the paper's FAN_1) over EL. Theorem 3 proves WKL -> FAN_Delta over EL. All over EL (full induction), so left out of the facts (EL0 is the catalogue base); WKL -> FAN_Delta over EL + MP is also stated and also not over EL0.

statement.notation: There exists a function f that, given an index of a total 0-1 valued Turing machine M, outputs a DFA for SUBSEQ(L(M))
statement.name: Effective Higman's theorem for decidable languages (DFA for SUBSEQ)
statement.definition: There exists a function f that, when given as input an index of a total 0-1 valued Turing machine M, outputs the code for a DFA for SUBSEQ(L(M)), where SUBSEQ(A) is the set of subsequences of strings of A.
statement.facts: Theorem 9.1: not provable in RCA0 (false in the model of recursive sets, since the paper shows by Section 4 that any such function computes the double jump of the empty set). Not equivalent to WKL0: any omega-model of the statement contains the double jump of the empty set, while some omega-model of WKL0 does not (remark attributed to an anonymous referee). Not equivalent to any usual system other than RCA0, since {X : X <=_T emptyset''} is an omega-model of it. Whether 'for any A, SUBSEQ(A) is regular' (Higman's theorem H, catalogue id higman) has a given strength is not answered by the paper.

statement.name: Fixed points of positive arithmetic operators
statement.definition: The second-order schema (FP): for every arithmetic formula phi(x, Y) in which Y occurs only positively (number and set parameters allowed), there is a set Y with forall x (x in Y <-> phi(x, Y)). FP0 is the system consisting of (FP), the basic quantifier-free axioms of PA and Sigma^0_1 induction.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.1: ATR0 and FP0 are equivalent (the proof derives (ATR) from (FP) by taking a fixed point of a positive formula coding the hierarchy, and (FP) from ATR0 by pseudohierarchies). Theorem 4.1: ATR0 is conservative over ID^<omega (iterated inductive definitions, a first-order theory) for arithmetic sentences, via cut elimination. Theorem 5.3: ATR0 has polynomial-length proofs of Con(ID_{2_n}) (speedup over ID^<omega).

statement.name: Theory of finitely iterated inductive definitions (fixed points, non-least)
statement.definition: The union of the first-order theories ID^_n in the language of Peano arithmetic with a predicate P_phi for each positive arithmetic operator phi, with axioms forall x (P_phi(x) <-> phi(x, P_phi)) and induction extended to the new language; ID^_{n+1} adds fixed-point constants for positive operators of the language of ID^_n.
statement.facts: Proof-theoretic ordinal Gamma_0 (Feferman); ATR0 is conservative over it for arithmetic sentences (Theorem 4.1); ATR0 proves Con(ID^_{2_n}) with short proofs (Theorem 5.3). It is a first-order theory, not a principle of the catalogue.

statement.name: Countable closed subsets of the circle are sets of uniqueness
statement.definition: Every closed countable C subset of S^1 is a set of uniqueness: the only trigonometric series vanishing on the complement of C has all coefficients 0.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Teorema 2 (iv)); the paper attributes the analysis to Humphreys [12] (Section 5.5). Humphreys also shows that the existence of the objects used in Cantor's original proof is equivalent to ATR0.

statement.name: Every open subset of R is Lebesgue measurable
statement.definition: Every open subset of R is Lebesgue measurable.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for Lebesgue measure on [0,1]
statement.definition: Dominated convergence theorem for Lebesgue measure on [0,1].
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Riesz representation theorem for positive linear functionals on [0,1]
statement.definition: Riesz representation theorem for positive linear functionals on [0,1].
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Unique divisible closure of countable abelian groups
statement.definition: Every countable abelian group has a unique divisible closure.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Hahn embedding theorem for ordered abelian groups
statement.definition: Every ordered abelian group embeds into a product of copies of (R, +, <) (Hahn).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Exponentiation of countable well-orderings
statement.definition: If a and b are countable well-orderings then a^b is a well-ordering (the line of the text shows "ab", exponent lost in extraction).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Girard; check the rendered PDF).

statement.name: Unique real closure of countable formally real fields
statement.definition: Every countable formally real field has a unique real closure.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Levi's theorem on torsion-free abelian groups
statement.definition: Every countable torsion-free abelian group is orderable.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Countable products of countable orderable groups are orderable
statement.definition: The countable product of countable orderable groups is orderable.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Domain of a Borel partial function is Borel
statement.definition: The domain of a Borel subset of R^2 with at most one value for each element is Borel.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Well-ordered sequences of countable well-orderings have a supremum
statement.definition: Every countable well-ordered sequence of countable well-orderings has a supremum.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Silver's theorem for Borel equivalence relations
statement.definition: Every Borel equivalence relation on R with uncountably many classes has a perfect set of pairwise inequivalent elements.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Pi11-CA0 over RCA0. The catalogue silver is stated for coanalytic relations.

statement.name: Norm-closed subspaces of l1 + c0 have a weak-closure
statement.definition: Every norm-closed subspace of l_1 (+) c_0 (symbols partly lost) has a closure in the weak topology.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Pi11-CA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Mal'tsev's theorem on ordered groups
statement.definition: Every countable ordered group has order type Z^a (+) Q^e with a a countable ordinal and e in {0,1} (symbols lost in extraction).
statement.facts: Equivalent to Pi11-CA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Determinacy of games with payoff a union of an open and a closed set
statement.definition: Games whose payoff set is the union of an open and a closed set are determined.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Pi11-CA0 over RCA0. Related to the catalogue sigma01-pi01-det (intersection of open and closed) by taking complements, not identical.

statement.name: G_delta sets have the Ramsey property
statement.definition: G_delta sets (countable intersections of open sets) have the Ramsey property.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Pi11-CA0 over RCA0.

statement.notation: WWKL0, RCA0 + omega^omega well ordered, ACA0', ACA0+, Pi11-TR0, Pi12-CA0
statement.name: The remaining systems among the eleven of Section 4
statement.definition: The paper lists the eleven systems RCA0, WWKL0, WKL0, RCA0 + "w^w well-ordered", ACA0, ACA0', ACA0+, ATR0, Pi11-CA0, Pi11-TR0, Pi12-CA0 in a (nearly) linear hierarchy; it says the first theorem equivalent to Pi12-CA0 was found recently (Mummert-Simpson [17]), and that WWKL0 is equivalent to several basic theorems of measure theory (note 12).
statement.facts: No theorem is stated about them besides these remarks; also Section 6: WKL0 is Pi02-conservative over PRA (Friedman, Sieg) and ATR0 proves the same arithmetical statements as the predicative theory IR (no loc given beyond Section 6). Not in the catalogue (conservation over PRA is not expressible with the base ids).

statement.notation: Every weakly represented family satisfying Angluin's condition (effectively / in the limit / generally) can be learnt in the limit
statement.name: Learnability of weakly represented families with Angluin's tell-tale condition
statement.definition: Statements 3-5 of Theorem 5: every weakly represented family satisfying Angluin's condition effectively (resp. in the limit, resp. generally) is learnable in the limit.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to DOM over RCA0 (Theorem 5); DOM is also equivalent to: the index set of every weakly represented family can be approximated in the limit.

statement.notation: Every uniformly represented family satisfying Angluin's condition with a general bound is learnable in the limit
statement.name: Learnability of uniformly represented families with a general Angluin bound
statement.definition: Every uniformly represented family satisfying Angluin's tell-tale condition with a general bound is learnable in the limit.
statement.facts: Equivalent to DOM over RCA0 (Theorem 7). Theorem 6: over RCA0 a uniformly represented family is learnable in the limit iff it satisfies Angluin's condition in the limit.

statement.notation: Every uniformly (weakly) represented family satisfying Angluin's tell-tale condition with a general bound is conservatively learnable
statement.name: Conservative learnability under Angluin's general bound
statement.definition: Statements 2 and 3 of Corollary 9: every uniformly (resp. weakly) represented family satisfying Angluin's tell-tale condition with a general bound is conservatively learnable.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Corollary 9).

statement.notation: Every weakly represented family with finite thickness (finite elasticity, characteristic subsets) is learnable in the limit
statement.name: Learnability criteria: finite thickness, finite elasticity, characteristic subsets
statement.definition: Every weakly represented family which has finite thickness (resp. finite elasticity, resp. admits characteristic subsets) is learnable in the limit.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to DOM over RCA0 (item 2 of Theorems 10, 11, 12); the uniformly represented case is provable in RCA0 (item 1).

statement.notation: Every member of a weakly represented family has a minimal index
statement.name: Minimal index principle for weakly represented families
statement.definition: In every weakly represented family, all its members have a minimal index.
statement.facts: Equivalent to IΣ2 over RCA0 (Proposition 16).

statement.name: Existence of a maximal almost disjoint family
statement.definition: There exists a weakly represented family of sets, pairwise almost disjoint, such that every infinite set B in S meets some member in an infinite set.
statement.facts: For omega-models, DOM is true iff MAD is false (attributed to [18]).

statement.notation: Hydra termination (extended Kirby-Paris hydra with ordinal labels <= omega)
statement.name: Termination of the rightmost-head hydra game for hydras labelled by ordinals up to omega
statement.definition: For every hydra A (finite labelled tree with root label +, other labels <= omega, nodes above the root labelled 0) and every sequence (n_i), there is k with A(n_0)(n_1)...(n_k) = ES, where A(n) results from chopping off the rightmost head.
statement.facts: Theorem I: true (proved by infinitary trees, Section 1). Theorem II: for each fixed hydra A the statement is provable in (Pi11-CA)+BI (Theorem 2.3). Theorem III: the Pi02 sentence 'for all n exists k A^n(1)...(k)=ES' is not provable in (Pi11-CA)+BI (via ID_omega, Theorem 4.0 and corollary).

statement.name: Pi11 comprehension plus bar induction
statement.definition: The second-order theory Pi11-CA together with the bar induction scheme BI; BI is not a catalogue statement (only Pi11 transfinite induction is).
statement.facts: The paper states it proves the same arithmetic sentences as ID_omega and contains ID_omega; it does not prove the hydra sentence of Theorem III.

statement.name: Theory of nu-times iterated inductive definitions
statement.definition: Extension of Peano Arithmetic by predicates P^A_u for positive operator forms, with closure and induction axioms for u < nu.
statement.facts: ID_omega is contained in (Pi11-CA)+BI and proves the same arithmetic sentences; Theorem 2.2: 'a in W_0' is provable in ID_nu for terms a without symbols D_v, v > nu; Theorem 4.0 bounds provably total functions of ID_nu; Appendix: proof-theoretic ordinal of ID_nu equals sup of rk(D_0 D_nu^k 0).

statement.notation: Lindenbaum's Lemma (decidable sets of propositional formulas)
statement.name: Lindenbaum's lemma for classical propositional calculus, intuitionistic version
statement.definition: For every decidable set Γ of formulas: if for every α in the binary fan some initial segment αn is inconsistent, incomplete, does not contain Γ, or is open (Definitions 6.1-6.4), then Γ is contradictory.
statement.facts: Equivalent to the Fan Theorem, to propositional Completeness (every lying decidable set is contradictory) and to propositional Compactness (every lying decidable set has a finite lying subset), pairwise over WKV (Theorem 6.5). WKV is an intuitionistic second-order system (Kleene-Vesley without continuity and bar induction, full induction, unique choice, variables over sequences), not EL0 nor BISH, so these equivalences are not entered over a catalogue reduction.

statement.notation: Completeness / Compactness for decidable sets of propositional formulas
statement.name: Propositional completeness and compactness (decidable sets, lying = unrealizable)
statement.definition: Completeness: for every decidable set Γ of formulas, if Γ is lying (no valuation makes all of Γ true) then Γ is contradictory (proves A0 and not A0). Compactness: if Γ is lying then some finite subset of Γ is lying.
statement.facts: Each equivalent to the Fan Theorem over WKV (Theorem 6.5). Related to the catalogue entry completeness (a classical, second-order reverse mathematics statement) but the intuitionistic formulation here differs.

statement.name: Fan Theorem for arbitrary fans, shown equivalent to the Fan Theorem on the binary fan
statement.definition: For every fan beta and decidable bar gamma of beta there is m such that every path of beta meets gamma before m.
statement.facts: Proposition 2.3: equivalent in WKV to the binary-fan version (cited from Troelstra [7]). In the catalogue only the Cantor space versions fandelta and fanfull appear.

statement.name: Multi-sorted second order arithmetic SA
statement.definition: First-order theory with countably many sorts of set variables, Peano axioms, full induction, k-simple predicative comprehension and a choice axiom from sort k to sort k+1; SA_s is the fragment with sorts at most s (SA_0 is PA).
statement.facts: Mutually interpretable with PATr (Corollaries 4.2, 4.5); SA_{s+1} proves Con(SA_s) (Theorem 5.2). Metamathematical, no statement about catalogue principles.

statement.name: Multi-sorted second order arithmetic with restricted induction SAR
statement.definition: SA with the induction axiom restricted to formulas of the form n in x; the paper says SAR_1 is the same as ACA_0.
statement.facts: Corollary 4.3: SAR_s is interpretable in PATr_s. The identification SAR_1 = ACA_0 is only asserted informally in Section 3, so not recorded as a fact.

statement.name: Peano arithmetic with truth predicates PATr
statement.definition: PA extended with truth predicates Tr_k for formulas of the language of PATr_{k-1}, k = 1, 2, ...; PATr_s keeps only Tr_1..Tr_s.
statement.facts: Mutually interpretable with SA, fragmentwise equiconsistent with SA_s (Section 5); PATr_{s+1} proves Con(PATr_s) (Lemma 5.1).

statement.notation: The Uniform Boundedness Theorem (for topological vector spaces)
statement.name: Uniform boundedness theorem (Banach-Steinhaus) for sequences of continuous linear maps from an F-space into a topological vector space, in Bishop-style constructive mathematics
statement.definition: If (T_m)_m is a sequence of continuous linear mappings from an F-space E into a topological vector space F such that {T_m x | m in N} is bounded in F for each x in E, then (T_m)_m is equicontinuous. The paper proves the version for a separable F-space E and a separated topological vector space F (Theorem 6, assuming BD-N).
statement.facts: Theorem 7: over Bishop-style constructive mathematics (BISH), BD-N is equivalent to the uniform boundedness theorem for sequences of continuous linear mappings from a separable F-space into a separated topological vector space (item 2), and to the statement that the pointwise limit T of such a sequence is continuous (item 3: if Tx = lim T_m x exists for each x then T is continuous). Theorem 6 gives BD-N implies item 2. Remark 8: BD-N already follows from the restriction to sequences of compact self-adjoint operators on l2. Theorem 1 (no BD-N needed): if a bounded sequence (x_n) in an F-space E has {T_n x_n} unbounded in a separated TVS F, then {T_n x} is unbounded for some x in E (constructive contrapositive form, via the constructive Baire category theorem).

statement.notation: Pointwise limit of continuous linear maps is continuous (Banach-Steinhaus corollary)
statement.name: Continuity of the pointwise limit of a sequence of continuous linear mappings on a separable F-space
statement.definition: If (T_m)_m is a sequence of continuous linear mappings from a separable F-space E into a separated topological vector space F such that T x = lim_m T_m x exists for each x in E, then T is continuous.
statement.facts: Theorem 7: equivalent to BD-N (and to the uniform boundedness theorem, item 2) in Bishop-style constructive mathematics.

statement.name: Separated topological vector space (constructive notion)
statement.definition: A topological vector space E is separated if for each neighbourhood U of 0 there exist a neighbourhood V of 0 and an open set W such that E = U union W and V intersect W is empty.
statement.facts: Every TVS whose open base is compatible with a family of pseudometrics is separated. The reals R with the discrete topology being separated is equivalent to WLPO, so it cannot be shown constructively that R with the discrete topology is separated (Section 2, remark before Theorem 1).

statement.name: Boolean prime ideal theorem
statement.definition: Every nontrivial Boolean algebra (equivalently, every nontrivial distributive lattice) has a prime ideal / prime filter. Studied over ZF, not over RCA0.
statement.facts: Theorem 3: over ZF, BPI is equivalent to every consistent first-order theory having a complete semantic structure; Corollary 6: over ZF, BPI is equivalent to every consistent first-order theory having a nonempty Kripke model; Corollary 9: over IZF, completeness of Kripke semantics is equivalent to LEM + BPI. These are set-theoretic (ZF/IZF) results and fit no reduction of the catalogue, so no fact was entered.

statement.name: Countable comprehension
statement.definition: For arithmetical φ such that (∀n)(∃ at most one X ⊂ N)φ(X,n), there is Z ⊂ N such that (∀n)((∃X ⊂ N)φ(X,n) ↔ n ∈ Z).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (each of Σ11-SEP and countable comprehension), by [559, V.5], as stated in Section A.2.2.

statement.name: Uniform monotone convergence theorem
statement.definition: There exists Φ : (N → R) → R such that for any increasing sequence (x_n) in [0,1], Φ(λn.x_n) is the limit of (x_n).
statement.facts: Equivalent to (∃²) over RCA₀^ω (Theorem B.4.1).

statement.name: Uniform intermediate value theorem (zero functional)
statement.definition: There is Φ : (R → R) → R such that for continuous f : [0,1] → R with f(0) ≤ 0 ≤ f(1), f(Φ(f)) = 0; also the version restricted to Lipschitz continuous functions. Not the catalogue uivt (sequential IVT).
statement.facts: Both versions are equivalent to (∃²) over RCA₀^ω (Theorem B.4.6).

statement.name: Existence of a function [0,1] → R that is not Baire 1; Baire 1 closure under composition
statement.definition: There is a function f : [0,1] → R that is not Baire 1 (equivalently Baire 1 f, g with g ∘ f not Baire 1).
statement.facts: Both are equivalent to (∃²) over RCA₀^ω.

statement.name: Existence of boundaries of open/closed sets of reals
statement.definition: For any closed C ⊂ R (or open O ⊂ R) the boundary exists as a set; or there is a functional B mapping closed sets to their boundaries.
statement.facts: Each of the three versions is equivalent to (∃²) over RCA₀^ω (Theorem B.4.8).

statement.notation: Existence of H(x) = 1 if x > 0 else 0
statement.name: Existence of the Heaviside-type function H : R → R
statement.definition: The function H(x) := 1 if x >_R 0 and 0 otherwise exists.
statement.facts: Equivalent to (∃²) over RCA₀^ω; also equivalent to the existence of Φ : N^N → N^N (or → N) not (sequentially) continuous everywhere.

statement.name: Pincherle's theorem on [0,1] (locally bounded functions are bounded)
statement.definition: A locally bounded function f : [0,1] → R is bounded (distinct from the catalogue Cantor-space versions pito, pito2, pitu).
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL₀ over RCA₀^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem C.2.15) and over RCA₀^ω + NCC (Exercise B.5.6); not provable in Z₂^ω (Corollary I.3.33); provable in Z₂^Ω.

statement.name: Closed choice for sequences of non-empty closed sets of reals
statement.definition: For a sequence of non-empty closed sets (C_n) in R there is (x_n) with x_n ∈ C_n for all n.
statement.facts: Provable in Z₂^Ω; the restriction to codes is provable in WKL₀; not provable in Z₂^ω (Theorem I.3.32).

statement.name: Induction for Σ-formulas (∃f ∈ N^N)(Y(f,n)=0), and for formulas (∃f)(∀g)(Y(f,g,n)=0)
statement.definition: The induction axiom for the formulas φ(n) ≡ (∃f ∈ N^N)(Y(f,n) = 0) (Σ-IND), respectively (∃f)(∀g)(Y(f,g,n)=0) (IND_3).
statement.facts: Exercise B.3.43: Σ-IND implies IND_2 over ACA₀^ω; Exercise B.3.46: IND_3 implies IND_R over ACA₀^ω; Theorem B.3.45: ACA₀^ω + Σ¹₂-IND enumerates finite Σ¹₁ sets of reals.

statement.name: Cadlag functions on [0,1] are bounded
statement.definition: A cadlag function f : [0,1] → R is bounded.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA₀^ω + WKL₀ (via the excluded middle trick).

statement.name: Upper semi-continuous functions on [0,1] are bounded above
statement.definition: A usco function f: [0,1] -> R is bounded above.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA_0^omega to HBC_s (C.2.24(f)), the Heine-Borel theorem for open covers (C.2.24(c)), the Cantor intersection theorem and attaining maxima; equivalent to WKL0 over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}; not provable in Z_2^omega (Corollary I.3.33).

statement.name: Heine-Borel theorem for closed sets and sequences of basic open intervals
statement.definition: HBC_s restricted to sequences of basic open intervals (closed C subset [0,1] without code).
statement.facts: Z_2^omega cannot prove it (Corollary I.3.33); equivalent to WKL0 over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem C.2.24(i)).

statement.name: Vitali's principle (Principle C.2.47) restricted to function classes
statement.definition: For Psi: [0,1] -> R+ in a function class and epsilon>0, finitely many balls B(x_i,Psi(x_i)) have measure at least 1-epsilon.
statement.facts: For continuous, lsco, quasi-continuous, cadlag, U0, Baire 1 or continuous-outside-a-closed-null-set Psi, equivalent to WWKL over RCA_0^omega.

statement.name: Uniform convergence of Bernstein polynomials for continuous functions
statement.definition: For continuous f: [0,1] -> R, f(x) = lim B_n(f,x) uniformly.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA_0^omega; the third-order variants for cadlag/regulated functions (with QF-AC^{0,1}) are equivalent too (Theorem C.2.31).

statement.notation: Fundamental theorem of calculus for continuous functions
statement.name: FTC for continuous functions
statement.definition: For continuous f: [0,1] -> R, F(x)=int_0^x f exists and F' = f everywhere.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA_0^omega; variants for cadlag/regulated functions equivalent over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}.

statement.name: Boundedness of regulated functions on [0,1]
statement.definition: A regulated f: [0,1] -> R is bounded.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}, with about thirty variants (usco, lsco, quasi-continuous, cadlag, Baire 1...); not provable in Z_2^omega (Remark C.2.19).

statement.notation: Existence of an unbounded / non-regulated function
statement.name: Third-order existence statements equivalent to (exists^2)
statement.definition: There exists a function f: [0,1] -> R that is not regulated / not Baire 1 / not usco / not cliquish / unbounded / ...
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to (exists^2) over RCA_0^omega + WKL (WKL only needed for a few items).

statement.notation: Supremum principle for effectively Baire 2 functions (and effectively Baire n, net-Baire 1, EB2, effectively sico, ee-continuous, effectively measurable, effectively Baire measurable, effectively pseudo-continuous functions)
statement.name: Supremum principle for effectively Baire 2 (net-Baire 1, ...) functions
statement.definition: A bounded effectively Baire 2 function f : [0,1] -> R (double limit of continuous functions given with the double sequence) has a supremum; same for the other classes of Definition C.4.3 and for net-Baire 1 functions with their net.
statement.facts: Theorem C.4.5 (ACA0^omega): equivalent to Pi11-CA0 (items (a)-(j), with Sigma-IND for the version with L2-arithmetical / Sigma11 graphs); item (a): any bounded Sigma11,x class in Q has a supremum. Corollary C.4.6 (RCA0^omega + Sigma-IND): the Suslin functional (S^2) is equivalent to (exists^2) plus the existence of the supremum norm for effectively Baire 2 (or net-Baire 1) functions with their double sequence (net) as input. The use of (exists^2) in the base is necessary (ECF).

statement.notation: MCT for nets indexed by finite sequences of Baire space (Principle C.4.13)
statement.name: Monotone convergence theorem for increasing nets (x_w) in [0,1] indexed by (N^N)^* ordered by inclusion
statement.definition: An increasing net (x_w) in [0,1], indexed by the finite sequences of elements of Baire space ordered by inclusion, converges to a limit. May coincide with the catalogue entry mctnet (nets indexed by subsets of N^N): check the definition in the earlier part.
statement.facts: Corollary C.4.15 (ACA0^omega): equivalent to BOOT. Theorem C.4.14 (ACA0^omega): the restrictions to effectively Baire 2 nets, L2-arithmetical nets and Sigma11 nets are each equivalent to Pi11-CA0.

statement.notation: Cousin's lemma for effectively Baire 2 (effectively Baire n, net-Baire 1) gauges
statement.name: Cousin's lemma for effectively Baire 2 gauges
statement.definition: Every effectively Baire 2 gauge Psi : [0,1] -> R+ (same for effectively Baire n, n >= 2, and net-Baire 1) has a finite sub-covering of the canonical cover.
statement.facts: Theorem C.5.9 (ACA0^omega + Delta12-IND): equivalent to ATR0, and to Cousin's lemma for codes for Baire 2 functions.

statement.notation: Jordan decomposition for effectively Baire 2 BV functions (net-Baire 1)
statement.name: Jordan decomposition theorem for effectively Baire 2 functions of bounded variation
statement.definition: Every effectively Baire 2 (or net-Baire 1) f : [0,1] -> R in BV is the difference of two non-decreasing functions.
statement.facts: Theorem C.5.6 (ACA0^omega + IND2 + Sigma12-IND): equivalent to ATR0, and to: the points of discontinuity can be enumerated; the suprema sup_{[p,q]} f exist as a sequence; for Riemann integrable BV effectively Baire 2 f with integral 0 the points where f is non-zero can be enumerated. Theorem C.5.2 gives the L2-arithmetical / Sigma11 BV versions, Theorem C.5.8 the unordered sums versions (all equivalent to ATR0).

statement.name: Supremum principle for a function class Gamma
statement.definition: For bounded f : [0,1] -> R in Gamma there is F : Q^2 -> R with F(p,q) = sup_{x in [p,q]} f(x) for rational p,q in [0,1].
statement.facts: Theorem C.6.4 (ACA0^omega + IND0): implies NIN[0,1] for Gamma = sigma-continuous, Baire 2, B-measurable of class 1, cliquish, regulated, usco, BV (also restricted to pointwise discontinuous, continuous a.e. or Riemann integrable functions). Theorem C.6.6 (ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} + IND2): the existence of a functional Phi with Phi(f) = sup f for bounded Baire 1 f implies NIN[0,1]. Theorem C.3.11 / C.2.15 give the Baire 1 case (WKL0).

statement.notation: Jordan decomposition restricted to usco BV functions; other restrictions of third-order theorems (Fsigma closure, unordered sums, Baire 2 open sets)
statement.name: Variations of third-order theorems implying NIN[0,1]
statement.definition: Restrictions of statements known from the Big Five (Jordan decomposition for usco BV functions, Cousin lemma for BV/regulated/usco/cliquish/sigma-continuous/Baire 2 gauges, existence of a point of continuity of regulated or usco functions, convergence of positive bounded unordered sums over [0,1], closure of Fsigma sets, interior of Gdelta sets, open Baire 2 sets have RM-codes).
statement.facts: All imply NIN[0,1] over ACA0^omega + IND0 (Theorems C.6.1, C.6.4, C.6.5, C.6.8, C.6.14-C.6.17) or over ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorems C.6.19, C.6.20; C.6.6 with IND2); Theorem C.6.17 also uses Pi11-CA0. Theorem C.6.13: Z2^omega cannot prove that regulated functions are Riemann integrable; the item "a function BV on every closed interval is effectively Riemann integrable" implies NIN[0,1] over ACA0^omega + IND0. Corollary C.6.11: ACA0^omega + ATR0 + Delta12-IND proves there is no effectively Baire n injection [0,1] -> Q.

statement.notation: Theorem C.3.17 / C.3.18: Baire 1 and net-Baire 1 preimages of open intervals
statement.name: Preimages of open intervals under Baire 1 functions
statement.definition: For Baire 1 f : [0,1] -> R and open interval I, f^{-1}(I) is F_sigma (with RM-codes under WKL0).
statement.facts: Theorem C.3.17 (RCA0^omega): equivalent to (exists^2): there is a Baire 1 f and I with f^{-1}(I) not open (or Fsigma but not open). Theorem C.3.18 (ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}): for net-Baire 1 f, f^{-1}(I) is Delta11.

statement.name: Arzelà's convergence theorem for the Riemann integral
statement.definition: If f and f_n are Riemann integrable on [0,1], f_n converges pointwise to f and |f_n(x)| <= M+1 for all n, x, then the integrals of f_n converge to that of f.
statement.facts: Theorem D.2.6: Arz implies NIN over ACA_0^ω. Remains valid with weaker conclusions (limit exists; metastability, Arz^-), Exercise D.2.7.

statement.name: No injection from R (resp. Baire space) to N
statement.definition: NIN_X: there is no injection Y: X -> N for X = R or Baire space N^N.
statement.facts: Theorem D.2.2: over ACA_0^ω, NIN_[0,1] <-> NIN_R <-> NIN_{N^N} <-> NIN_{2^N}.

statement.notation: NIN_bv, NIN_Y, NIN_Riemann, NIN_Borel, NIN_reg, NIN_cliq, NIN_semi, NIN'_semi
statement.name: No injection from [0,1] to Q of a given regularity class
statement.definition: No injection from [0,1] to Q that has bounded variation / property Y / is Riemann integrable / Borel / regulated / cliquish / usco / lsco.
statement.facts: Theorem D.2.3: over ACA_0^ω + IND_0 each is equivalent to NIN_[0,1] (IND_0 only needed for the last five).

statement.name: No bijection from R / Cantor space / Baire space to N
statement.definition: NBI_X: no bijection Y: X -> N.
statement.facts: Theorem D.2.42: Z_2^ω cannot prove NBI_{2^N}. Theorem D.2.45 (ACA_0^ω): NBI_[0,1] <-> NBI_R and NBI_[0,1] -> NBI_{N^N}.

statement.name: No bijection from [0,1] to Q (or to [0,1] ∩ Q) of a given regularity class
statement.definition: Variants of NBI with total variation 1, Riemann integrable, cliquish, usco, lsco bijections.
statement.facts: Theorem D.2.46: over ACA_0^ω + IND_0 each is equivalent to NBI_[0,1].

statement.name: NCC with only an upper bound on m
statement.definition: NCC where g in Principle B.5.5 only provides an upper bound on the m-variable.
statement.facts: Corollary D.2.44: RCA_0^ω + NCC_w proves NBI_[0,1].

statement.name: The unit interval is not height-width countable
statement.definition: A set B is height-width countable if there are a height function H and a width function g with |{x in B: H(x)<n}| <= g(n) for all n (each such set finite).
statement.facts: Theorems D.2.69 and D.2.73 (ACA_0^ω + IND_2): equivalent to many properties of BV-functions (unordered sums, Waterman variation, Fourier series). Theorem D.2.67: Jordan decomposition theorem for [0,1], HBU and WHBU restricted to BV imply NIN'_alt. Theorem D.2.75: NIN_alt <-> NIN'_alt over ACA_0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} + Y for Y any of the unifying principles (p.1)-(p.7) of Principle D.2.74. Theorem D.2.77: equivalent to Volterra-style statements for BV over ACA_0^ω + Helly. The book says NIN'_alt is not provable in Z_2^ω + QF-AC^{0,1}.

statement.name: Helly's selection principle (growth of variations)
statement.definition: If (f_n) are BV [0,1]->[0,1] functions with pointwise limit f not in BV, then there is unbounded g in N^N with g(n) <= V(f_n) <= g(n)+1.
statement.facts: Theorem D.2.77: over ACA_0^ω + Helly, NIN_alt is equivalent to Volterra-type statements for BV (Bf = Q impossible, a continuity point exists, Bernstein polynomials converge). The book believes Helly does not imply NIN_[0,1].

statement.name: Basic properties of the Jordan measure
statement.definition: There is a functional J: (R -> N) -> R with J(empty)=0, J([a,b]) = b-a and countable additivity on rudimentary sets.
statement.facts: Exercise D.2.24: RUD implies NIN_[0,1].

statement.name: Kannan's fixed point theorem on [0,1]
statement.definition: On a complete metric space M = [0,1], a map T with d(Tx,Ty) <= b(d(x,Tx)+d(y,Ty)), b<1/2, has a fixed point.
statement.facts: Exercise D.2.36: NIN_[0,1] follows from it over ACA_0^ω.

statement.name: Range principle range0
statement.definition: For any A ⊂ [0,1] and Y : [0,1] → N injective on A, there is B ⊂ N with n ∈ B ↔ (∃x ∈ A)(Y(x)=n).
statement.facts: Theorem D.3.6: cocode0 ↔ range0 over ACA₀^ω; ACA₀^ω + range0 proves ATR₀ (Principle A.2.7).

statement.name: Countable chain condition ccc (disjoint open intervals can be enumerated)
statement.definition: Let A ⊂ R² be such that distinct intervals (a,b), (c,d) in A are disjoint; then A can be enumerated.
statement.facts: Exercise D.3.32: cocode0 ↔ ccc over ACA₀^ω (left as exercise).

statement.name: Comparability of height-countable well-orders
statement.definition: For height-countable well-orders (X, ⪯X), (Y, ⪯Y) with X, Y ⊂ R, one is order-isomorphic to the other or to an initial segment, or vice versa.
statement.facts: Theorem D.3.29: ACA₀^ω + Σ-IND proves enum ↔ CWO^ω.

statement.name: Supremum principle for countable RSC-spaces; separability / Lindelöf property of countable RSC-spaces
statement.definition: Third-order countable second-countable (RSC) spaces: a countable RSC-space is separable (or Lindelöf), or the supremum principle holds for continuous functions on compact countable RSC-spaces.
statement.facts: Theorem D.3.34: all equivalent to cocode0 over ACA₀^ω; Exercise D.3.35: height-countable analogues equivalent to enum.

statement.name: Coding principle for D-open sets (and related D-closed principles)
statement.definition: Every D-open set O ⊂ R (union of sets Jn each an open interval or union of two) has an RM-code.
statement.facts: Theorem D.3.39: equivalent over ACA₀^ω to cocode0, to existence of λx.d(x,C) for D-closed C, to the supremum principle for D-usco functions, and to Urysohn for D-closed sets.

statement.name: Baire category theorem for open sets with an R2-representation
statement.definition: BCT[0,1] restricted to open dense sets given with an R2-representation (a function Y with B(x, Y(x)) ⊂ O for x ∈ O).
statement.facts: Theorem D.4.3: provable in ACA₀^ω. Consequently Z₂^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} cannot prove that regulated f has a sequence of R2-representations of (Dk) (Theorem D.4.4).

statement.name: Numerical choice for Π¹₁ formulas (ENC)
statement.definition: For any φ ∈ Π¹₁, (∀n)(∃m)φ(n,m) implies (∃g ∈ N^N)(∀n)φ(n,g(n)); ENC^ω is its generalisation to higher-order parameters.
statement.facts: Over RCA₀, ENC ↔ ATR₀ (Theorem I.4.16, cited from the book); ACA₀^ω + ENC^ω conservative over ATR₀ (Theorem I.2.10); Theorem D.4.7: ACA₀^ω + ENC^ω proves BCT[0,1].

statement.name: Points of continuity of usco functions (semi-continuity lemma)
statement.definition: For usco f : [0,1] → R (possibly with an oscillation function, or countably continuous), there is x ∈ [0,1] where f is continuous; also: usco f is bounded below on some interval.
statement.facts: Theorem D.4.9: each is equivalent to BCT[0,1] over ACA₀^ω. Theorem D.4.13: provable in ACA₀^ω for usco f with a modulus; Theorem D.4.15: for pointwise limits of continuous functions.

statement.name: Every usco function f : [0,1] → R is Baire 1
statement.definition: Any usco function f : [0,1] → R is Baire 1.
statement.facts: Corollary D.4.16 (ACA₀^ω): implies BCT[0,1] and open. Corollary D.4.34: "any fragmented function is Baire 1" also implies BCT[0,1] and open.

statement.name: Uniform boundedness principle for lsco functions
statement.definition: A sequence of lsco functions pointwise bounded on [0,1] is uniformly bounded on some (c,d) ⊂ [0,1].
statement.facts: Theorem D.4.24: equivalent to BCT[0,1] over ACA₀^ω.

statement.name: Points of continuity of cliquish functions with oscillation function; concentration of discontinuity
statement.definition: For cliquish (or fragmented, sequentially sico, B-measurable class 1) f : [0,1] → R with an oscillation function there is a point of continuity; for totally discontinuous f with oscillation function there are N, c, d with oscf ≥ 2^-N on (c,d).
statement.facts: All equivalent to BCT[0,1] over ACA₀^ω (D.4.26 and D.4.27 also with QF-AC^{0,1}, D.4.33 with IND_R). Theorem D.4.32: BCT[0,1] follows from the existence of a modulus of cliquishness; NINalt from these items restricted to regulated functions. Theorem D.4.28/D.4.30: quasi-continuous versions provable in ACA₀^ω.

statement.name: Volterra theorem, Volterra corollary and Blumberg theorem for usco, cliquish or sigma-continuous functions
statement.definition: There are no two pointwise discontinuous (or cliquish, or usco) functions with oscillation functions whose continuity and discontinuity points are exchanged; no such function continuous on Q ∩ [0,1] and discontinuous on the irrationals; Blumberg for usco functions.
statement.facts: Theorem D.4.36: equivalent to BCT[0,1] over ACA₀^ω; Theorem D.4.37: provable in ACA₀^ω for quasi-continuous functions.

statement.name: The set Bf (points where the Bernstein polynomials converge to f) is non-empty for usco or cliquish f
statement.definition: For usco f : [0,1] → R (or cliquish with an oscillation function), the set Bf is non-empty.
statement.facts: Theorem D.4.38: equivalent to BCT[0,1] over ACA₀^ω.

statement.name: Weak Baire category theorem (measure one open sets)
statement.definition: If (On) is a decreasing sequence of measure one open sets of reals in [0,1], then ∩ On is non-empty.
statement.facts: Theorem D.5.2: equivalent over ACA₀^ω + IND_R + QF-AC^{0,1} to Hankel/Dini continuity-point statements for Riemann integrable usco functions, FTC, Volterra for Riemann integrable functions, concentration of oscillation (statement truncated at the end of the task text).

statement.name: Variants of enum: enum′ (height-width countable sets), cocode0 for sets and the Jordan/supremum items
statement.definition: Equivalent formulations of enum: sup of regulated functions exists as a sequence, Df enumerable for regulated f, mesh formulation, Jordan decomposition for BV on R; with Y from Principle D.2.74 enum ↔ Y + Jordan etc.
statement.facts: Theorems D.3.7 and D.3.13 (over ACA₀^ω + QF-AC^{0,1}), D.3.16, D.3.24 (non-enumerable closed set has a limit point), D.3.26 (Cantor characterisation of η).

statement.name: Axiom of choice for sequences of non-empty finite sets of reals
