statement.definition: Let (X_n) be a sequence of non-empty finite sets in [0,1]. Then there is (x_n) with x_n in X_n for all n.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega + IND_2: QF-AC^{0,1} implies it and it implies finite-Sigma^1_1-AC_0 (Theorem E.3.2, E.4.1); it follows from many properties of sequentially compact, connected or compact metric spaces (Theorems E.2.2, E.2.5, E.2.11, E.2.15).

statement.name: Finite Choice with a bound on the size of the sets
statement.definition: Finite Choice for (X_n) with g in N^N such that |X_n| <= g(n).
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega: QF-AC^{0,1} implies it, it implies width-Sigma^1_1-AC_0 (Corollary E.3.3).

statement.name: Width Sigma^1_1 choice
statement.definition: finite-Sigma^1_1-AC_0 where a bound g(n) >= length of the finite sequence of witnesses is given.
statement.facts: Sigma^1_1-AC_0 -> finite-Sigma^1_1-AC_0 -> width-Sigma^1_1-AC_0 -> weak-Sigma^1_1-AC_0 (Section E.1.2); a system of hyperarithmetical analysis.

statement.name: ClC for decreasing sequences of sequentially closed sets
statement.definition: ClC formulated for sequences (C_n) of sequentially closed sets with C_{n+1} subset C_n.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega + IND_2: QF-AC^{0,1} -> ClC_seq -> weak-Sigma^1_1-AC_0, ClC_seq equivalent to R is a sequential space (RSeq), sup C in C for sequentially closed C, boundedness of sequentially usco functions, a Heine-Borel principle for sequentially open sets (Theorems E.5.2, E.5.8); strictly weaker than QF-AC^{0,1}.

statement.name: Quantifier-free dependent choice for functions
statement.definition: For quantifier-free phi: (forall n)(forall f)(exists g) phi(n,f,g) -> (exists (f_n))(forall n) phi(n,f_n,f_{n+1}).
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega equivalent to the Baire category theorem for complete metric spaces M subset N^N and R2-open dense sets, and to usco/cliquish functions with oscillation function not being totally discontinuous (Theorem E.2.18); Z_2^omega + QF-DC^{1,1} does not prove NIN[0,1] (Corollary I.3.40, quoted).

statement.name: QF-AC^{0,1} for finitely many (unique) witnesses
statement.definition: QF-AC^{0,1}_{fin} with unique existence in the antecedent.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega, cocode_1 is equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1}_{!fin} together with GS for strongly countable RSC-spaces (Theorem E.2.23).

statement.notation: PHP[0,1] variants (Vitali-Lebesgue, FTC, concentration of discontinuity)
statement.name: Statements equivalent to Tao pigeonhole principle for closed sets
statement.definition: Items such as: for Riemann integrable f with oscillation function the set D_f has measure 0; the fundamental theorem of calculus almost everywhere; Bernstein approximation holds almost everywhere.
statement.facts: Equivalent to PHP[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_R + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorems D.5.9, D.5.10); ACA_0^omega + PHP[0,1] is Pi^1_2-conservative over ACA_0 (Theorem D.5.11, not recorded: conservation over ACA_0 is not expressible).

statement.name: Bounded numerical choice (second order, Π^1_1 formulas)
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR_0 over RCA_0 (Theorem E.7.8, items (e),(f), by Theorem I.4.16); equivalent over ACA_0^ω + IND_2 to domination statements for sub-continuous / Riemann integrable functions restricted to effectively Baire 2 or net-Baire 1 functions (Theorem E.7.8).

statement.name: Bounded numerical choice with higher-order parameters
statement.loc: Principle E.5.14 and the text after it
statement.definition: BNC with higher-order parameters (arithmetical matrix in the proof of Theorem E.5.15: (∀n)(∃m)(∀f ∈ 2^N)ψ(n,m,f)).
statement.facts: Theorem E.5.15 (ACA_0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1}): equivalent to: a sub-continuous f: R→R is dominated by a continuous g; same for everywhere Riemann integrable f; modulus of Riemann integration; locally bounded; restrictions to simply continuous or Baire measurable functions. Theorem E.5.20 (Sanders-Taranovsky [541]): ACA_0^ω + BNC^ω proves NIN_[0,1]. The book says Z_2^ω + ∪_σ QF-AC^{σ,1} cannot prove BNC (Theorems I.3.22 and I.3.39, outside this part). Implies BCT_[0,1] over a slightly extended base (Corollary G.4.43, outside this part).

statement.name: A sub-continuous function f: [0,1] → R is bounded (together with IND_2)
statement.definition: Sub-continuity as defined earlier in the book; the principle states boundedness on [0,1].
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^ω: QF-AC^{0,1} ↔ (sub-continuous functions on [0,1] are bounded + IND_2) (Corollary E.5.11); also for sequential split continuity, for sequentially closed C ⊂ [0,1], and for the extreme value theorem for sequentially split continuous functions. Over RCA_0^ω: IND_2 + this principle ↔ QF-AC^{0,1} + (continuous functions on [0,1] are bounded) ↔ QF-AC^{0,1} + (locally bounded functions on [0,1] are bounded) (Theorem E.5.13).

statement.name: Kőnig infinity lemma for graphs on subsets of R (original form)
statement.definition: Korg0: graph with countable vertex set V = ∪ V_n ⊂ R, each V_n finite non-empty, each vertex of V_{n+1} adjacent to one of V_n; then there is a path (v_n) with v_n ∈ V_n. Korg1: V strongly countable. Korg2: sequence of finite non-empty sets E_n ⊂ R with a relation R.
statement.facts: Theorem E.6.2 (ACA_0^ω): Korg1 → NBI_[0,1]. Corollary E.6.3 (ACA_0^ω): Korg1 ↔ cocode_1. Theorem E.6.5 (ACA_0^ω): [QF-AC^{0,1} + IND_3] → Korg2 → cocode_1.

statement.name: Higher-order ascending-descending sequence principle for infinite linear orders on subsets of R
statement.definition: Every infinite linear ordering (X, ⪯_X) with X ⊂ R (item (b)), with X countable (item (c)), with X strongly countable (item (d)) has an increasing or decreasing sequence in X.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^ω + IND_2: QF-AC^{0,1} ↔ item (b) → (c) → (d) ↔ cocode_1 (Theorem E.6.7).

statement.name: Properties of positive convergent unordered sums over [0,1]
statement.definition: (b) for a positive convergent unordered sum there is a sequence of reals outside which a_y = 0; (c) a modulus of convergence exists.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^ω + IND_1: QF-AC^{0,1} → (b) ↔ (c) → cocode_1 (Theorem E.6.10).

statement.name: Restrictions of the sequential-continuity theorems to effectively Baire 2 (or net-Baire 1) functions
statement.definition: E.g. an effectively Baire 2 f: R→R is continuous at x iff sequentially continuous there (E.7.1(b)); a sub-continuous effectively Baire 2 f: [0,1]→R is bounded (E.7.3(b)); Baire category theorem for complete L^2-arithmetical (M,d), M ⊂ N^N, with Σ^0_1-defined dense open sets (E.7.10).
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^ω + IND_2: Theorem E.7.1 (b),(c) and Theorem E.7.3 (b),(c),(d) are each equivalent to Σ^1_1-AC_0. Over ACA_0^ω: the items of Theorem E.7.10 are equivalent to Σ^1_1-DC_0. Theorem E.7.8 (a)-(d) are equivalent to BNC and ATR_0 over ACA_0^ω + IND_2.

statement.name: Generalised bootstrap principles
statement.definition: BOOT_2: for Y: (N^N × N^N) → N there is X ⊂ N with n ∈ X ↔ (∃f)(∀g)(Y(f,g,n)=0); BOOT_k adds k-1 quantifier alternations.
statement.facts: BOOT_2 → Π^1_1-CA_0 over RCA_0^ω and ACA_0^ω + BOOT_2 proves Π^1_2-CA_0 (noted after Principle F.2.19); BOOT_k → Π^1_k-CA_0 over RCA_0^ω and ACA_0^ω + BOOT_k proves Π^1_{k+1}-CA_0 (noted after Principle F.2.21). BOOT_2 follows from the supremum principle F.2.18 (Theorem F.2.20) and BOOT_k, k ≥ 2, likewise (Corollary F.2.22).

statement.name: Supremum principles for continuous functions on sequentially compact metric spaces (M, d), M ⊂ N^N
statement.definition: Existence of the sequence of suprema over balls (F.2.11), of the suprema of a sequence of continuous functions (F.2.12), or of the supremum function x ↦ sup_y f(x,y) for Lipschitz f on N^N × N^N (F.2.18); the metric d: (N^N)^2 → R is a third-order object.
statement.facts: Theorem F.2.14 (ACA_0^ω + Σ-IND): F.2.11 restricted to f: M → [0,1] ↔ F.2.12 restricted to [0,1] ↔ BOOT (also for Lipschitz f and limit point / countable / open cover compactness). Corollary F.2.16 (ACA_0^ω): BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1} ↔ QF-AC^{0,1}_fin + F.2.12. Theorem F.2.20: F.2.18 → BOOT_2. Theorem F.2.26 (RCA_0^ω): (∃³) ↔ (∃²) + existence of the supremum functional on such spaces.

statement.notation: Metric-space statements equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} or BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1}
statement.name: Third-order statements on compact metric spaces (M, d), M ⊂ N^N
statement.definition: Sequentially compact implies separable / bounded / countably compact; countable sets can be enumerated; closed measure zero sets are effectively measure zero; boundedness, extreme value and Dini for continuous functions; Sierpiński classification of countable metric spaces without isolated points; open_0, open_1, open_2 (open sets are countable unions of balls).
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^ω + Σ-IND: those about separability, enumerability of countable sets, effective measure zero, Sierpiński's theorem and open_i imply or are equivalent to BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorems F.2.1, F.2.6, F.2.10, F.2.30). Over ACA_0^ω: the bounded / countably compact / extreme value / Dini versions together with QF-AC^{0,1}_fin are equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorems F.2.4, F.2.15), and the strongly countable versions are equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem F.2.8).

statement.name: Finite quantifier-free choice QF-AC^{0,1}_fin (called IND_2 in other publications of Sanders)
statement.definition: For quantifier-free φ with (∀n)(∃f ∈ N^N)φ(f,n): (∀k)(∃(f_n)_n)(∀n ≤ k)φ(f_n,n).
statement.facts: Not matched to the catalogue ind23 (which uses Y of type 2, f ∈ 2^N and a different hypothesis shape); used as a conjunct throughout Section F.2. A human should decide whether it equals ind23.

statement.name: Fourth-order generalisations of BOOT, RANGE and QF-AC to metric spaces M ⊂ N = N^N → N^N
statement.loc: Principle F.2.35, Theorem F.2.37, Theorem F.2.40
statement.definition: BOOT^2_1: for Z^3 there is f ∈ N^N with f(n)=0 ↔ (∃Y ∈ N)(Z(Y,n)=0).
statement.facts: Z_2^Ω + BOOT^2_1 proves comprehension for Π^2_1 formulas (text after Principle F.2.35). Theorem F.2.37 (Z_2^Ω): supremum principle F.2.36 restricted to [0,1] ↔ BOOT^2_1 ↔ RANGE^2. Theorem F.2.40 (ACA_0^ω): QF-AC^{0,1→1} ↔ QF-AC^{0,1→1}_fin + (bounded / countably compact / intermediate value theorem / Lipschitz boundedness on sequentially compact M ⊂ N).

statement.notation: RSC-space statements (SUP, SUP', MAX, separability, Lindelöf)
statement.name: Third-order statements on compact RSC-spaces
statement.definition: Supremum and maximum principles and boundedness of continuous functions on (sequentially) compact RSC-spaces.
statement.facts: Theorem F.3.5 (ACA_0^ω): QF-AC^{0,1} ↔ QF-AC^{0,1}_fin + boundedness of continuous functions on sequentially compact RSC-spaces ↔ existence of a strongly extensional discontinuous function on strongly infinite ones ↔ sequentially compact implies countably compact ↔ attainment of the supremum.

items.quote:

0 + A0 + IND2 + HBU proves ATR0 ,
items.paperNotation: ACA0^omega + A0 + IND2 + HBU proves ATR0
items.concerns: IND2 (Definition B.3.38) identified with ind23; A0 is Definition G.4.12 (catalogue a0); ACA0^omega is RCA0^omega + (E2). Proof goes through Sigma-SEP (not in catalogue).

items.quote:
⋄ Π11 -CAω
0 + A0 + IND2 + HBU proves Π2 -CA0 .
items.paperNotation: Pi11-CA0^omega + A0 + IND2 + HBU proves Pi12-CA0
items.concerns: Pi11-CA0^omega is RCA0^omega + (S^2) (Section B), entered as suslin; IND2 identified with ind23. The book derives it from Pi11-CA0^omega + Sigma-SEP proving Pi12-CA0 (Theorem D.3.5).

statement.name: Bootstrap principle with k-1 quantifier alternations
statement.definition: For Y^2 there is X subset of N with n in X <-> (exists f)(forall g)(Y(f,g,n)=0) (BOOT_2), generalised to k-1 alternations.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega + BOOT_k proves Pi^1_k-CA_0 and ACA_0^omega + BOOT_k proves Pi^1_{k+1}-CA_0 (stated as recalled). BOOT_2 follows from the supremum principle for graph continuous [0,1]^2 -> [0,1] functions (Theorem F.4.21, over ACA_0^omega); BOOT_k (k>=3) likewise (Corollary F.4.22); SUP2 -> BOOT_k for k>=2 (Theorem F.3.11).

statement.name: Supremum principle for compact RSC-spaces X x Y in R^2
statement.definition: For compact RSC-space X x Y and continuous f : X x Y -> [0,1], there is Phi : X -> R^2 with Phi(x)(1)=sup_y f(x,y), Phi(x)(2)=inf_y f(x,y).
statement.facts: SUP2 -> BOOT_k for all k>=2 over ACA_0^omega (Theorem F.3.11).

statement.notation: RSC-space principles (separable, Lindelof, SUP, MAX, SUP')
statement.name: Basic properties of RSC (real second-countable) spaces
statement.definition: Separability, Lindelof property, supremum principle SUP (and SUP'), maximum principle MAX for RSC-spaces.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}_fin, the following are equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} + BOOT (conjunction boot-qfac01): RSC-spaces are separable, Lindelof, compact RSC-spaces are separable, SUP, SUP', their restrictions, MAX (Theorem F.3.8). Over RCA_0^omega, (exists3) is equivalent to (exists2) plus a supremum functional for continuous functions on compact RSC-spaces (Theorem F.3.9). Equivalences between QF-AC^{0,1} and boundedness / sequential compactness properties of RSC-spaces in Theorem F.3.5 (earlier part). Ginsburg-Sands for RSC-spaces X subset R is provable in ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem F.3.6); GS in the catalogue is for CSC spaces.

statement.notation: supremum principle / functional for weakly continuous functions (graph continuous, Young, almost continuous, ...)
statement.name: Supremum principle and supremum functional for classes Gamma of weakly continuous functions
statement.loc: Principle F.4.12, Definition F.4.2, Principle F.4.19
statement.definition: Principle F.4.12: sup_{x in [p,q]} f(x) exists as a sequence over p,q in Q for f in Gamma; Definition F.4.2: functional Xi : (R->R)->R with Xi(f)=sup f for f in Gamma; Principle F.4.19: lambda x. sup_y f(x,y) exists for f : R^2 -> R in Gamma_2.
statement.facts: Over RCA_0^omega, (exists3) is equivalent to (exists2) + supremum functional for Gamma in {Young condition, almost continuity (Husain), graph continuity, not of Cesaro type, peripheral, pre-, C-continuity} (Theorem F.4.3); same for P-decision functionals (Theorem F.4.5). Over ACA_0^omega, BOOT is equivalent to the supremum principle for all R->R functions and for the graph continuous classes (Theorem F.4.13); with Sigma-IND, also to the supremum for continuous a.e., Riemann integrable, cliquish, pointwise discontinuous, simply continuous, measurable functions (Theorem F.4.16). For the tame classes of Definition F.4.8 (alpha-, s-, A-, AB-, quasi-, contra-, RC-, SR-continuity) the supremum functional is provable in ACA_0^omega (Theorem F.4.9), and with (exists2) replaced by FF (Theorem F.4.10). Pi^1_1-CA_0 is equivalent to the effectively Baire 2 version (Theorems F.5.7, F.5.11); Suslin functional S^2 equivalent to (exists2) + supremum norm for bounded effectively Baire 2 graph continuous functions (Exercise F.5.10).

statement.name: Evaluation of the Riemann integral for weakly continuous functions
statement.definition: For f : R -> R in Gamma and p,q in Q, the Riemann integral of f on [p,q] can be evaluated (sequence in R u {+inf,-inf,undefined}).
statement.facts: Equivalent to BOOT over ACA_0^omega for graph continuous functions and the classes of Definition F.4.8 (Theorem F.4.15).

statement.name: Every open set of reals is F_sigma
statement.definition: An open set of reals is Fsigma (without RM-codes).
statement.facts: Does not imply NIN[0,1] or NBI[0,1]; combined with other principles gives equivalents of open (Theorems G.3.8, G.3.22).

statement.notation: Supremum / maximum principle for usco functions; usco functions are Baire 1
statement.name: Properties of upper semi-continuous functions on [0,1]
statement.definition: Supremum (resp. maximum) principle for usco f : [0,1] -> R, usco functions are Baire 1, supremum for bounded B-measurable functions of class 1 together with open^dagger.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}, each is equivalent to open (Theorem G.3.8). Supremum principle for continuous functions on closed sets C (Principle G.3.18) is equivalent to open over ACA_0^omega (Theorem G.3.19). open -> HBU_usco (HBU restricted to usco Psi) over ACA_0^omega (Theorem G.3.17).

statement.notation: Urysohn lemma / Tietze extension theorem for closed sets of R (third-order, no codes)
statement.name: Third-order Urysohn lemma and Tietze extension theorem
statement.definition: Urysohn: for disjoint closed C0,C1 subset R there is continuous g : R -> [0,1] with x in Ci <-> g(x)=i; Tietze: continuous f on closed C extends to R.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}, each of Urysohn, (weak Urysohn + open^dagger), (Tietze + open^dagger) is equivalent to open (Theorem G.3.22); QF-AC^{0,1} only needed for item (b).

statement.name: Lindelof lemma for closed sets of R; open covering principle OC_{0,0}
statement.definition: LIN(R): for closed C subset R and Psi : R -> R+, a sequence (x_n) in C with the balls B(x_n,Psi(x_n)) covering C. OC_{0,0}: for increasing open sets O_n, if every [-n,n] is inside some O_m then there is g with [-n,n] inside O_{g(n)}.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} + OC_{0,0}: LIN(R) -> open (Theorem G.3.33). Over ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}: open is equivalent to OC_{0,0} + LIN(R) for continuous (BV, usco) Psi (Corollary G.3.34); (LIN(R)+OC_{0,0}) <-> (HBU + open) (Corollary G.3.35).

statement.name: Lindelof lemma for arbitrary subsets of Baire space (LIN); sequential Lindelof lemma for N^N
statement.definition: LIN: for G^2 and non-empty D subset N^N, a sequence (f_n) in D with the basic sets [fbar_n G(f_n)] covering D. LIN_seq(N^N): sequential version for N^N.
statement.facts: ACA_0^omega + LIN_seq(N^N) proves Pi^1_1-CA_0 (Theorem G.4.2, also for lsco sequences, Corollary G.4.3). Over ACA_0^omega, LIN <-> BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem G.4.6), also for continuous G (Corollary G.4.7); the Lindelof lemma for arbitrary C subset R (also continuous, BV Psi) is equivalent to BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem G.4.8); Pi^1_1-CA_0 <-> LIN restricted to effectively Baire 2 sets D and continuous G (Theorem G.4.9).

statement.name: Uncountable unions of open sets are open
statement.definition: For Psi : N^N -> R^2 there is an open O with x in O <-> x in union over f of (Psi(f)(1),Psi(f)(2)).
statement.facts: Exercise G.3.5 asks to show ACA_0^omega + UO proves BOOT (not proved in the text).

statement.name: Arithmetical version of the coding principle open
statement.definition: Arithmetical formulas phi that are extensional and open have codes: phi(x) <-> exists n (a_n < x < b_n).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR_0 over ACA_0 (Theorem I.2.13, cited); equivalent over ACA_0^omega + IND_2 + Sigma^1_2... (Sigma_2-IND) to restrictions of usco/Baire/Urysohn/Tietze to effectively Baire n sets (Theorem G.3.41).

statement.notation: Sigma^1_1-AC_0 equivalents (metric spaces with effectively Baire 2 metrics)
statement.name: Boundedness/compactness of (N^N,d) for effectively Baire 2 metrics
statement.definition: Sequentially compact (N^N,d) with d effectively Baire 2 is bounded / weakly countably compact; intermediate value and boundedness theorems restricted to L2-arithmetical M and effectively Baire 2 d, f.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to Sigma^1_1-AC_0 over ACA_0^omega + IND_2 (Theorem F.5.2).

statement.name: Every function in ACG (ACG*) is differentiable at some point; complement of ACG (ACG*) dense in C([0,1])
statement.definition: Variants of Banach's theorem on nowhere differentiable functions for the classes ACG and ACG*.
statement.facts: Not provable in Z_2^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem G.2.2), since each implies NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0 (NIN[0,1] is not provable there by Theorem D.2.1, other part).

statement.name: Lindelof lemma for arbitrary subsets of Baire space
statement.definition: For any G^2 and non-empty D subset of N^N, there is a sequence (f_n) in D such that the union of the [f_n-bar G(f_n)] covers D.
statement.facts: Theorem G.4.6: over ACA0^omega, LIN <-> [BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1}]; Corollary G.4.7: the equivalence holds restricted to continuous G.

statement.name: Lindelof lemma for arbitrary subsets of the reals
statement.definition: For any C subset of R and Psi: R -> R+, there is a sequence (x_n) in C such that the union of B(x_n,Psi(x_n)) covers C.
statement.facts: Theorem G.4.8: over ACA0^omega, equivalent to BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1}, also when restricted to continuous Psi and to continuous BV Psi. Theorem G.4.9: restricted to effectively Baire 2 sets D and continuous G it is equivalent to Pi11-CA0 over ACA0^omega.

statement.name: Higher-order Sigma11 separation (third-order, with type-2 parameters)
statement.definition: For i = 0,1 and arithmetical psi_i, phi_i(n) = (exists f_i in N^N) psi_i(n,f_i): if no n satisfies both phi_0 and phi_1, there is Z subset of N containing every n with phi_0(n) and no n with phi_1(n). Proofs use type-2 parameters Y, so it is not the second-order sigma11-sep.
statement.facts: Theorem G.4.14: ACA0^omega proves Sigma-SEP -> cocode0. Corollary G.4.15: ACA0^omega proves Sigma-SEP^-_C <-> cocode0. Theorem G.4.17: ACA0^omega + A0 proves [HBU + bounded-Sigma-SEP] -> Sigma-SEP; Corollary G.4.18: ACA0^omega proves [HBT + bounded-Sigma-SEP] -> Sigma-SEP. Pi11-CA0^omega + Sigma-SEP proves Pi12-CA0 (Theorem D.3.5).

statement.name: Axiom A1 (universal version of the fragment of NFP)
statement.definition: For Y^2 and A(sigma) = (forall f in 2^N)(Y(f,sigma)=0): (forall f in N^N)(exists n)A(f-bar n) -> (exists Phi^2)(forall f in N^N)A(f-bar Phi(f)).
statement.facts: Theorem G.4.25: RCA0^omega + A1 proves continuous F: 2^N -> N has a continuous modulus. Theorem G.4.27: ACA0^omega + A1 proves HBU -> HBCs. Theorem G.4.28: RCA0^omega + A1 + HBU proves Pincherle's theorem. A1 implies the Baire category theorem for [0,1] over ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (Exercise G.4.31).

statement.name: Higher-order numerical choice
statement.definition: Numerical choice principle of Section E.5.4 (definition not in the examined part).
statement.facts: Theorem G.4.16: over ACA0^omega + Sigma-IND, ENC^omega implies HBT. Theorem G.4.42: ENC^omega + open-dagger implies open over ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}.

statement.name: Uniform weak Konig lemma
statement.definition: (forall G^2)(exists m)(forall T subset 2^<N)[(forall f in 2^N)(f-bar G(f) not in T) -> (forall g in 2^N)(g-bar m not in T)]. Not the catalogue uwkl.
statement.facts: Theorem G.4.50: over ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}, Cousin's lemma for Cantor space (hbuc), WKL^u and the uniform Heine theorem are equivalent.

statement.name: WHBU for arbitrary subsets E of [0,1]
statement.definition: For Psi: [0,1] -> R+, eps > 0 and non-empty E subset [0,1] of measure e there are x_0..x_k in E with the measure of the union of B(x_i,Psi(x_i)) at least e - eps.
statement.facts: Theorem G.4.60: over ACA0^omega, WHBU <-> WHBU+_RM <-> WHBU+.

statement.notation: Lindelof lemma for general open coverings of R
statement.name: Lindelof lemma for general open coverings
statement.definition: For a mapping x |-> O_x with O_x open containing x, there is a sequence (x_n) with the union of the O_{x_n} covering R.
statement.facts: Theorem G.4.58: ACA0^omega proves it implies cocode0. Theorem G.4.62: ACA0^omega proves cocode0 follows from the Lindelof lemma for fixed radius interval coverings of closed sets in R.

statement.name: Numerical choice for increasing sequences of open sets
statement.definition: For an increasing sequence of open sets (O_n) in R: (forall n)(exists m)([-n,n] subset O_m) -> (exists g)(forall n)([-n,n] subset O_{g(n)}).
statement.facts: Theorem G.5.7: over RCA0^omega, WKL0 + OC^{0,0} is equivalent to the sequential Heine-Borel theorem and to usco functions on R being bounded above by continuous functions together with WKL0. Theorem G.5.8: Z2^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} cannot prove OC^{0,0}; Z2^Omega proves it.

statement.name: Continuity-testing functional on Baire space
statement.definition: (exists Z^3)(forall Y^2)[Z(Y)=0 <-> (forall f)(exists N)(forall g)(f-bar N = g-bar N -> Y(f)=Y(g))].
statement.facts: Theorem G.6.2: over RCA0^omega + WKL + QF-AC^{2,0}, (kappa_0^3) <-> (Z^3) + FF. Corollary G.6.3: (E3) <-> (E2) + (Z^3) over RCA0^omega; Theorem G.6.10: (Z^3) <-> [(E3) or not (E2)] over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{2,0}.

statement.name: Littlewood-type principles and WHBU restricted to measurable functions
statement.definition: Lusin (LUS, LUS'), Egorov (EGO), Littlewood LLP and weak Egorov WTE theorems for measurable functions; WHBU_m is WHBU for measurable Psi.
statement.facts: Over ACA0^omega (+ QF-AC^{0,1} for LUS and EGO^-): LUS <-> LUS_RM and LUS -> WHBU_m; LUS' -> WHBU_m; EGO^- <-> EGO^-_RM and EGO^- -> WHBU_m; LLP <-> LLP_RM and LLP -> WHBU_m; WTE -> WHBU_m (Theorems G.4.65-G.4.73).

statement.name: Splittings and disjunctions of WKL, Z3, FF, MUC, HBU, WHBU
statement.definition: Equivalences involving disjunctions and negations such as WKL <-> [(E2) or HBU], WWKL <-> [(E2) or WHBU], MUC <-> [WKL + (kappa_0^3) + not (E2)], FF <-> [(E2) or MUC], LIN_R <-> [HBU or not WKL].
statement.facts: Theorems G.6.5, G.6.9-G.6.11, G.6.19, G.6.21-G.6.22 and Corollaries G.6.7, G.6.12-G.6.17, G.6.23-G.6.25; these use disjunction and negation of principles, which the database cannot express, and the statements T0, T1 (Section G.6.3.1) not in the catalogue.

statement.name: Weak non-monotone inductive definition principle (WNMI0)
statement.definition: For Y^2 and F(A) := A ∪ {Y(A)}, there is B ⊂ N with F(B) ⊆ B and (∀n ∈ B)(∃A ⊊ B)(Y(A)=n).
statement.facts: Theorem G.8.3: RCA0^ω proves WNMI0 → NIN[0,1] (via NIN_{2^N} and Theorem D.2.2). Exercise G.8.4 (not proved): BOOT implies WNMI0; cocode0 implies a restricted form.

statement.name: Weak non-monotone inductive definition principle (WNMI1)
statement.facts: Theorem G.8.6: ACA0^ω + WNMI1 proves second-order ATR0 (via Avigad's FP0, [18, Theorem 3.1]). Exercise G.8.7: provable for continuous F in RCA0^ω; RCA0^ω + WKL0 + WNMI1 does not prove ACA0. Remark G.8.9: QF-AC^{2,1} suffices to get a functional for WNMI1.

statement.name: Fixed point principle for monotone F: 2^N → 2^N
statement.definition: For monotone F: 2^N → 2^N, (∃A ⊂ N)(F(A) =_1 A).
statement.facts: Conjecture only: Z2^ω + FP0^ω cannot prove NIN[0,1].

statement.name: Existence of the range of type three functionals
statement.facts: MCT for nets in [0,1] indexed by N (= N^N → N) implies RANGE^1 ([525, Theorem 3.38]); Theorem G.7.4 generalises to index sets of any finite type.

statement.name: Height-countable subsets of [0,1] have measure zero
statement.definition: A height-countable set A ⊂ [0,1] has measure zero (Harnack).
statement.facts: Theorem G.10.3 (ACA0^ω): follows from enum or from PHP[0,1]; implies NINalt; "countable sets of reals have measure zero" follows from WHBU. Theorem G.10.4 (ACA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1}): equivalent to "for regulated f: [0,1] → R, the set D_f has measure zero". Theorem G.10.7 (ACA0^ω): strengthened (effectively measure zero) version implies de la Vallée-Poussin-type uniqueness theorem (b) which implies NINalt. Exercise G.10.6: equivalent to a uniform bound ε<1.

statement.name: Surjection, connected metric space, perfect set and complete metric space forms of the uncountability of R
statement.definition: Theorem G.11.2: (b) f: X → [0,1] surjective implies X uncountable; (c) a connected A ⊂ M with |A| ≥ 2 is uncountable; (d), (e) f(M) uncountable for connected M, continuous f; (f) surjective image of a metric space onto a connected one; (g) connected functionally Hausdorff RSC spaces. Theorem G.11.4: (b) perfect sets of reals are not countable; (c),(d) complete metric spaces without isolated points are uncountable; (e),(f) the same for images under (sequentially) continuous maps.
statement.facts: Theorem G.11.2 (ACA0^ω + QF-AC^{1,1}): each of (b)-(g) is equivalent to NIN[0,1] (item (d) without QF-AC^{1,1}). Theorem G.11.4 (ACA0^ω + QF-AC^{1,1} + (R1)): (b)-(f) equivalent to NIN[0,1] ((R1) not needed for item (d)).

statement.name: Cantor's theorem: for A ⊂ [0,1] and Y: [0,1] → N injective on A there is x ∈ [0,1] \ A
statement.definition: As named in the title.
statement.facts: The book states that "a manipulation of definitions shows that NIN[0,1] and Cantor's theorem are equivalent" (no base given); N-reduction facts with HBU (Theorem G.9.7) use a notion of reduction not in the catalogue.

statement.notation: Supremum of usco functions with modulus
statement.name: Existence of sup of usco functions with modulus of usco
statement.definition: A functional Φ with Φ(f,g) = sup_{x ∈ [0,1]} f(x) for all usco f: [0,1] → R with modulus of usco g.
statement.facts: Theorem G.11.8: ACA0^ω + HBU + QF-AC^{2,1} proves it.

statement.name: Notion of reduction among third-order statements
statement.definition: A reduction relating problems (∀Y^2)(∃x^1)A(Y,x) via Turing machines with oracle and terms of Gödel's T.
statement.facts: Theorem G.9.4 (J(Y) existence and monotone nets in Cantor space strongly N-reduce to one another), G.9.5, G.9.6, G.9.7: reductions of HBU, NIN[0,1], Lebesgue number lemma to net convergence, NFP, HBU restricted to Baire class 2. Not a reduction of the catalogue; nothing entered.

statement.name: Cantor-Bendixson theorem for closed sets of reals (third-order, countable = injection to N)
statement.definition: A closed C ⊂ R is the disjoint union of a perfect closed set P and a countable set S, where countable means there is an injection into N.
statement.facts: Theorem H.3.7: Z_2^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} + CBT does not prove NIN[0,1]; ACA_0^ω + CBT does not prove ATR_0 (via Theorems I.3.20, I.3.21, where the model satisfies not-NIN[0,1], so CBT holds vacuously). The coded second-order CBT is equivalent to Π^1_1-CA_0.

statement.name: Perfect set theorem for closed sets of reals (third-order, countable = injection to N)
statement.definition: For any uncountable closed set C ⊂ R there is a perfect set P ⊂ C; countable means injection to N.
statement.facts: Theorem H.3.7: Z_2^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} + PST does not prove NIN[0,1]; ACA_0^ω + PST does not prove ATR_0. May coincide with the catalogue entry perfect-set, whose definition (analytic sets) differs; not matched.

statement.name: Countable linear orders and well-orderings in the sense of (H.6)
statement.definition: (X, ⪯_X) with X ⊂ R is a CLO if it is a linear order and there is Y : R → N such that Y(x) = Y(y) implies x =_X y for x, y in X; a CWO is a well-ordering with this property.
statement.facts: Theorem H.3.10 (ACA_0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1}): BOOT is equivalent to "a CLO (X, ⪯_X) with X ⊂ R is order-isomorphic to a subset of Q". Exercise H.3.13: over the same base BOOT is equivalent to the comparability of CWOs.

statement.name: Supremum principle for compact CRSC-spaces
statement.definition: For a compact RSC-space X that is a CRSC-space (there is Y : R → N with Y(x) = Y(y) implying x and y topologically indistinguishable), a continuous f : X → R and a decreasing sequence (C_n) of closed non-empty sets, there is a sequence (x_n) with x_n = sup over C_n of f.
statement.facts: Theorem H.3.17 (ACA_0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1}): BOOT is equivalent to SUP for CRSC-spaces. Exercise H.3.22: Ginsburg-Sands theorem for CRSC-spaces is equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} over ACA_0^ω + IND_2.

statement.name: Kőnig infinity lemma over sets with an equivalence relation
statement.definition: For sets E_n of (X, =_X) that are finite (Definition H.3.23) and non-empty, and a binary relation R such that every x in E_{n+1} has some y in E_n with yRx, there is a sequence (x_n) with x_n in E_n and x_n R x_{n+1}.
statement.facts: Theorem H.3.25: over ACA_0^ω, Korg3 implies QF-AC^{0,1} and QF-DC^{1,1}. Corollary H.3.26 (ACA_0^ω): Korg3 is equivalent to QF-DC^{1,1}.

statement.name: A union over N of enumerable sets of reals is enumerable
statement.definition: For a sequence (A_n) of enumerable sets of reals, the union of the A_n is enumerable.
statement.facts: Not provable in Z_2^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} but provable in Z_2^Ω + QF-AC; it implies enum, and the weaker statement "R is not a union over N of enumerable sets" implies NIN_alt (hence is not provable in Z_2^ω + QF-AC^{0,1}).

statement.name: Arithmetical Baire category theorem
statement.definition: For an arithmetical formula φ(x,n) in L2 respecting =_R such that each {x : φ(x,n)} is open and dense, there is z with φ(z,n) for all n; also for any complete separable metric space without isolated points and for Baire space.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to its versions for complete separable metric spaces and for Baire space and to the existence of Σ0_n-generic elements of Cantor/Baire space relative to every Z (Theorem I.2.15, due to an anonymous MathOverflow user [481]); provable in ACA0 and, over RCA0, it does not imply WKL0 (Theorem I.2.16); ACA0^ω + BCT[0,1] is conservative over ACA0.

statement.name: Domination of limsup of continuous functions supported on at most one point per unit interval
statement.definition: Every R→R function that is the lim sup of a sequence of continuous functions and is non-zero for at most one argument on each unit interval is dominated by a continuous function.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem I.4.16, Taranovsky).

statement.notation: CL_B2 (Cousin's lemma for codes for Baire 2 functions)
statement.name: Cousin's lemma for Baire class 2 gauges (codes)
statement.definition: Cousin's lemma (every gauge on Cantor space/[0,1] admits a finite subcover) for gauges given by codes for Baire class 2 functions (equivalently Δ⁰₃-definable, Lemma I.4.20).
statement.facts: Theorem I.4.22 (ACA0): Cousin's lemma for codes for Baire 2 functions implies ATR0 (proofs taken from Barrett [30] and Barrett–Downey–Greenberg [31], 'Cousin's lemma in second-order arithmetic'). The catalogue has cousin-b1 and cousin-c but not the Baire 2 version.

statement.notation: Item (B) of Section I.4.5 (supremum functional Psi)
statement.name: Existence of a supremum functional for continuous functions on [0,1]
statement.definition: There is Ψ : (R→R)→R such that for continuous f:[0,1]→R, (∀x∈[0,1])(f(x) ≤ Ψ(f)) and (∀k)(∃y∈[0,1])(f(y) > Ψ(f) − 1/2^k).
statement.facts: Theorem I.4.11: RCA0^ω + (B) is conservative over WKL0 (via MUC and Theorem I.2.8). Theorem I.4.13: RCA0^ω + MUC_classic proves (B). The attaining version, item (A) (Φ with f(x) ≤ f(Φ(f))), is equivalent to (∃²) over RCA0^ω (Exercise B.4.12, an earlier chapter).

statement.name: Fan functionals Ξ and ξ
statement.facts: Stated as exercises: RCA0^ω + Ξ is conservative over WKL0; RCA0^ω + ξ is not conservative over WKL0 and the existence of ξ is equivalent to (∃²).

statement.notation: Finite closed sets have measure zero (ACA0)
statement.name: Closed finite subsets of Cantor space have measure zero
statement.definition: Every code for a closed finite set C ⊂ 2^N has measure zero.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0 (Schweber [565]). With ACA0^ω + Σ-IND, finite sets of reals have measure zero (Exercise B.3.44). Section I.5 notes that 'a countable set of reals has measure zero' is implied by cocode0 together with PHP[0,1].

statement.notation: Jeřábek's finite epsilon-net for closed sets
statement.name: Closed sets in [0,1] are covered by finitely many epsilon-balls centred in the set
statement.definition: For any code for a closed E ⊂ [0,1] and ε>0 there are x_0,…,x_k in E with E covered by the union of the balls B(x_i, ε).
statement.facts: Provable in WKL0 (Jeřábek [311]); sequential version is Exercise I.4.18.

statement.notation: Net-Baire 1 functions are Borel; jointly/separately continuous representation
statement.name: Theorems I.4.25-I.4.27 (descriptive set theory, not RM principles)
statement.definition: I.4.25: a pointwise limit of a net of continuous functions indexed by (N^N, ≤1) is Borel. I.4.26 (RCA0^ω+ACA0): for jointly continuous F: N^N x R → R, F(α,x)>y is Σ⁰₁. I.4.27 (ACA0^ω): separately continuous F is a pointwise limit of jointly continuous F_n and F(α,x)>y is Σ⁰₃.
statement.facts: Not comparisons of catalogue statements.

statement.name: Weak Baire category theorem, Cousin's lemma for usco functions, 'open sets are Fσ'
statement.definition: WBCT[0,1] studied in Section D.5.2; HBU_usco is Cousin's lemma restricted to usco functions; open† says an open set of reals is Fσ.
statement.facts: Section I.5 recalls: WBCT[0,1] is implied by BCT[0,1] and by PHP[0,1]; HBU_usco follows from open (Theorem G.3.17) and implies NIN[0,1]; open† follows from open but does not imply NIN[0,1] or NBI[0,1]. These are recalled from other chapters and not entered here.
